Firstly, the improved idea of Alpha-IOU is introduced into SIOU to construct a new exponential SIOU loss function (E- SIOU), which introduces more nonlinear properties in the target detection task, suppresses the error propagation and accelerates the model convergence, and makes it more sensitive in calculating the bounding box overlap degree; Secondly, the An attention mechanism that operates through multiple dimensions is introduced(MCA), which takes into account To model the importance of multi-dimensional cooperation in a novel way, improving performance while incurring little additional computational overhead; Subsequently, the EMA attention mechanism is used to construct a new C2f-E module in the feature extraction network, which groups the channel dimensions into multiple sub-features and reshapes some of the channel dimensions into batch dimensions to maximise the feature information of the small targets for the purpose of improving the detection accuracy. Finally validated on the VisDrone-2019 dataset, the experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper has a 3% improvement in mAP@0.50 compared to YOLOv8s algorithm and a 1.9% improvement in mAP@0.50:0.95.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Interaction Techniques Based on Device Digital Twin Model
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: As an important part of digital twin, two-way interaction technology enables the digital twin model to communicate and control information with the actual device in a two-way and dynamic way. Firstly, the XML-based file format is used to construct the digital twin model, deeply analyze the model hierarchy and node relationship, and carry out correct nesting and hierarchization according to the organization structure of the actual object. Secondly, with reference to the digital twin 3D model, a three-layer architecture of application-communication-device is proposed for two-way interaction, which maps the device motion state to the digital twin model in real time, and at the same time controls the device motion state through peripheral devices in the visualization interface. In this paper, we take a six-axis robotic arm as an example to model the robotic arm with high precision and explore the key technology of digital twin two-way interaction.

articleTitle: Towards Spatio-Temporal Aware Real Location Restoration for Signaling Data
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This study introduces the novel problem of Real Location Restoration, aimed at reconstructing accurate user trajectories from the coarse-grained mobile signaling data. To tackle this problem, we propose the Spatio-Temporal Aware framework for Signaling Data (STASD), a pioneering approach that encodes the complex spatiotemporal relationships of cellular trajectories. Leveraging a unique global transition graph, STASD captures high-order spatial relationships to effectively mitigate the Ping Pong Effect, a common issue in signaling data analysis. Our extensive experiments showcase the framework’s capability to accurately restore real-world trajectories, significantly advancing the field of mobile data analysis by providing a novel method to interpret and utilize signaling data for detailed location insights.

articleTitle: Optimization strategy for variable cycle engine control plan based on improved group search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The fuel consumption rate is one of the key control parameters for aircraft engines. In order to simultaneously optimize the fuel consumption rates at multiple cruise points for variable cycle engines, this paper proposes an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm. Under the premise of ensuring the safety constraints of variable cycle engines, the fuel consumption rates of the engine are optimized offline for multiple steady-state operating points, including both subsonic and supersonic conditions. Based on the optimization results, the original control schedule of the engine is refitted and adjusted, resulting in a new control schedule table. This enables the online scheduling of optimized control plans for different operating conditions, ensuring the optimal fuel consumption rates at multiple steady-state operating points. Numerical simulation experiments demonstrate a decrease in fuel consumption rate by 15.12% at a certain subsonic cruise point and by 2.4% at a certain supersonic cruise point.

articleTitle: Research on Small Object Detection Based on Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence technology has made small object detection a recent focus and challenge in tasks such as unmanned aerial vehicles, aviation, and foreign object detection at airports. The main challenges lie in the small receptive fields of networks, which make it difficult to obtain sufficient target features, and the lack of abstract semantic information in lower-level features, which hinders accurate object localization. Furthermore, existing models suffer from densely sampled, fixed-size manually designed bounding boxes, which are not conducive to detecting small objects. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a small object detection algorithm based on feature fusion and attention mechanism. The main contributions are as follows: firstly, in the Neck stage, lightweight and efficient convolutional attention modules, as well as simple and effective RepVGG modules, are introduced to make the network focus more on useful information and enhance feature fusion capabilities. Secondly, in the Head stage, a new feature fusion method called ASFF is introduced, and additional small object detection heads are added to detect small objects in lower-level feature networks. The prediction heads can adaptively learn the fusion spatial weights for each scale feature map. Finally, experimental results show that on the VisDrone 2019 dataset, compared to state-of-the-art small object detection algorithms, the proposed algorithm improves the average precision by 5.26%, accuracy by 6.80%, and recall by 4.09%.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral image classification based on cross-domain adaptive broad learning system
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification is crucial for the identification of terrestrial objects in the field of remote sensing. The complexity and cost associated with annotating these images present significant challenges, as obtaining high-quality labeled samples is essential for the accuracy of classification. To address this challenge, this study proposes an innovative method for hyperspectral image classification, known as the Cross-Domain Mean Adaptive Broad Learning System (CDMABL). This approach initially employs cross-domain mean approximation within the feature mapping process of the Broad Learning System (BLS) to minimize the differences in marginal and conditional distributions between the source and target domains. To further enhance the model's generalization capabilities, domain adaptation terms are strategically integrated into the output layer of the BLS framework. Subsequently, ridge regression is utilized to optimize the model's output weights. The robustness and effectiveness of this algorithm are demonstrated through its successful application and validation on three distinct hyperspectral image datasets.

articleTitle: Projection-Based Iterative Learning Control for Linear Systems With Flexible Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In practical applications of iterative learning control (ILC), the desired trajectory may scale within different time intervals along the iteration axis, leading to the non-uniform trial length problem. To solve the problem, this paper proposes a projection-based ILC algorithm for linear time-varying systems with flexible tasks. Defining the system dynamics in Hilbert space, the performance index to be iteratively optimized is designed through a successive projection strategy. Based on this performance index, a norm optimal ILC algorithm is obtained, and the convergence analysis of the proposed algorithm is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by numerical simulation of a gantry robot.

articleTitle: Prediction model of Bum-through Point based on GA-BP
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: As one of the important links in the traditional long process steel production process, the sinter yield and quality of the sintering process directly affect the efficiency of ironmaking production. As an important index to detect the sintering production status, the sintering end point is very important for optimizing the production process and improving the product quality. Predicting the sintering end point can help the production planning and scheduling work, and make the production process more orderly and efficient. Accurate endpoint prediction helps to optimize production schedules and ensure the right raw materials and energy inputs to meet the quality requirements of a specific products. A prediction model of BTP based on GA-BP was proposed in this paper. Based on the production data of an iron and steel enterprise, the anomalies in the production data were processed. Then the genetic algorithm (GA) was used to set the initial value and threshold of the neural network (BP), and a GA-BP prediction model was designed. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the GA-BP model for the sintering end point can reach more than 95 %. The sintering prediction ability is further optimized, which effectively suppresses the fluctuation of the sintering end point, improves the calculation accuracy of the sintering end point, assists the field staff to adjust the operating parameters in advance, and stabilizes the sintering production. It has important theoretical significance and practical value in production practice.

articleTitle: An enhancing multiple kernel extreme learning machine based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Kernel extreme learning machine(KELM) embeds raw data into high-dimensional feature space through predefined kernel functions to analyze and process data and has advantages in learning speed and generalization ability. Deep neural network(DNN) provide more effective data mapping capabilities than shallow kernel functions. In this article, we introduce a universal algorithm that combines DNN and KELM, named Multi Deep Kernel Extreme Learning Machine(MDKELM). It applies multi kernel learning methods to combine the mapping matrices of different layers of DNN and applies the obtained optimal kernel matrix to KELM. The experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the advantages and potential of this method.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Multi-agent Predefined time Tracking Control Based on Dynamic Scaling Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In response to the challenges of individual agents within heterogeneous multi-agent formation tracking control unable to acquire global information and facing difficulties in rapid convergence due to unknown external disturbances, a strategy for global Predefined time control of multi-agent formation based on time-varying scale functions and dynamic scale factors is proposed. Firstly, a distributed Predefined time observer is designed to enable multi-agent systems to rapidly estimate the target state under communication constraints. Secondly, an adaptive fixed-time disturbance observer is designed to estimate unknown external disturbances in the system. The dynamic scale factor eliminates strict restrictions on system information imposed by external disturbance thresholds, and the upper bound of disturbance convergence time is independent of the initial state. Finally, a Predefined time controller based on Predefined time convergence rate and nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode surface is designed to achieve Predefined time tracking control of multi-agent formation. The superiority of the proposed control strategy is theoretically demonstrated and validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: ITM-SLAM: Instance-Level Semantic Tracking and Mapping in Dynamic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) constitutes a critical component of mobile intelligent robotics. However, it often faces challenges due to the influence of dynamic objects in many scenarios. Consequently, to address these challenges, this paper introduces an instance-level semantic SLAM algorithm, ITM-SLAM. It advances in visual odometry, data association, and nonlinear optimization to effectively handle dynamic objects. Initially, a visual odometry based on object detection and point cloud clustering is designed, alongside edge detection for accurately delineating the boundaries of dynamic objects. Moreover, to estimate the motion of dynamic objects, the algorithm employs the Kalman filter. Additionally, it designs a strategy for object allocation to facilitate data association. In terms of optimization, this paper proposes an optimization method based on ellipsoid and dynamic feature, integrating dynamic objects into the overall optimization framework. Experimental evaluation conducted on the TUM dataset demonstrates that the algorithm proposed in this paper significantly enhances localization accuracy in comparison with various SLAM algorithms.

articleTitle: CMF-Net: Semantic Segmentation of 3D Color Point Clouds in Outdoor Scenes for Intelligent Wheelchairs Based on Multimodal Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been significant development in intelligent wheelchair technology, making advances in autonomous navigation, path planning, obstacle detection, and obstacle avoidance. Point cloud semantic segmentation, as a core technology for intelligent wheelchairs to perceive their surrounding environment, has become a hot topic of research. Due to the complexity of outdoor environments, traditional 3D point cloud semantic segmentation methods often struggle to accurately identify targets with similar shapes. This results in a negative impact on the navigation and safety performance of intelligent wheelchairs. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a novel semantic segmentation method of 3D color point clouds in the outdoor environment for intelligent wheelchairs by using the LiDAR and camera. This approach generates comprehensive six-dimensional color point cloud data, effectively capturing both the three-dimensional spatial and color information of outdoor scenes. Furthermore, this paper proposes a semantic segmentation network of 3D color point clouds based on multimodal fusion, called CMF-Net. It is designed to deeply integrate spatial and color features from this data, significantly enhancing the color point cloud semantic segmentation capabilities of intelligent wheelchairs. The proposed CMF-Net consists of three modules: the feature extraction module, the feature fusion module, and the feature resolution module. the feature extraction module extracts features from position, feature, and color information. This enhances the network’s ability to capture various types of information from color point cloud, thereby improving its performance. The feature fusion module processes and merges features from the feature extraction module, providing the point cloud with both local and global features. Its key advantage is the integration of an efficient channel attention (ECA) module, enhancing the focus on critical information for improved network accuracy. The feature resolution module calculates category probabilities for each point from the fused features, completing point cloud semantic segmentation. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CMF-Net exhibits superior performance in outdoor environments, achieving a remarkable accuracy rate of 98.10%. Compared to PointNet, our method shows a 10% increase in accuracy, while it surpasses PointNet++ and DGCNN by 3.37% and 2.97% respectively. The proposed CMF-Net significantly enhances semantic segmentation accuracy for 3D colore point clouds. This improvement elevates outdoor environmental perception, thereby increasing the safety of intelligent wheelchairs.

articleTitle: Model predictive admittance control of knee arthroplasty surgical robot
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In addressing the issues of smooth tracking of surgeon-intended motion and surgical safety constraints for a semi-active knee arthroplasty surgical robot, this paper proposes a Model Predictive Admittance Control. Leveraging the compliant control mechanism based on the admittance model and integrating a Model Predictive Control algorithm with explicit constraint-handling capabilities, a composite admittance model predictive controller for the robotic arm is designed. The control robustness is enhanced through the rolling optimization and feedback correction features of the Model Predictive Control. A comparative experiment with a three-loop PID control is conducted to validate that the Model Predictive Control algorithm exhibits superior trajectory tracking performance, achieving desired admittance dynamics for enhanced compliance. Furthermore, the study extends to validate the active constraint effects of the composite admittance model predictive control on a robotic arm with strong coupling and complex system parameter structures.

articleTitle: Sinter Quality Prediction with Multimodal Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The accurate real-time estimation of the quality index of iron ore sintering is essential for maintaining the stability of the production process. To address the dynamic challenges and time delays inherent in the sintering process, a hybrid approach combining deep residual network (ResNet) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) for predicting the concentration of ferrous oxide (FeO) in sintering processes is developed. The proposed ResNet-LSTM model integrates the strengths of conventional models and is capable of processing multiple-modality data, including both image and time series. The efficacy of the proposed model is evaluated through experimental analysis using real-world data collected from the iron ore sintering process. The results indicate that the ResNet-LSTM model outperforms competing models, achieving the lowest prediction error rates.

articleTitle: Prediction model for furnace cylinder activity based on GRA-SSA-LSSVM
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Since entering the new century, China's iron and steel technology has developed rapidly, and the issue of blast furnace life has been increasingly valued by researchers. Furnace cylinder activity is considered to be the key factor affecting the life and stable anterograde of blast furnace, so reasonable prediction of furnace activity is of great significance to guide blast furnace production and improve blast furnace smelting efficiency. This paper proposes a furnace cylinder activity prediction model based on the GRA-SSA-LSSVM model. The pre-treated production data is used to obtain the quantified activity index of blast furnace cylinder by relevant formulas. Then the feature variables were selected by grey relational analysis combined with mechanism analysis. In order to further improve the prediction accuracy of the model, a furnace cylinder activity prediction model based on Sparrow search algorithm (SSA) optimized least square support vector machine (LSSVM) was proposed based on the above content, and the effectiveness of the predictive model was simulated and analyzed. The results show that the accuracy of predicting the cylinder activity using this method is high, which can meet the needs of guiding the actual production.

articleTitle: Radial Distortion Correction of UAV Images Based on Geometric Properties of PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) installation capacities increase both domestically and internationally. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology shows excellent potential in PV power plant inspection, especially in combination with infrared thermography, which provides an effective early fault detection method. However, images captured by UAVs may be affected by radial distortion, which causes straight lines in the images to become curved, affecting the accuracy of PV module identification and fault diagnosis. Since PV module have the geometrical property that the lines are parallel or perpendicular to each other, this paper proposes an image correction method based on this property, which evaluates the correction effect by calculating the number of parallel and perpendicular pairs of lines in the image. We use an iterative approach to adjust the distortion correction parameters. The proposed method effectively corrects the image distortion caused by camera lens while maintaining the integrity and accuracy of critical structures in the image. For experimental validation, we collected infrared thermal images using a UAV at a PV power plant in Jiangsu Province, China. Compared with existing methods, the method proposed in this paper has significant advantages in avoiding overcorrection and maintaining the structural integrity of PV modules, which can help in subsequent PV module identification and fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: MCMFuse:a Multi-level Co-selection Model in the Frequency Domain to Enhance EEG Signal Analysis for Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Electroencephalogram signals, as physiological signals unaffected by subjective consciousness and physiological dysfunctions, can objectively reflect a patient's physiological data and serve as a reliable basis for emotion recognition. Prior research has highlighted the temporal and spatial features of EEG signals. However, extracting frequency-domain features is difficult due to EEG's non-stationary. This study introduces an inception structure to reuse more EEG features. Then, we carry out an enhanced co-selection in the frequency domain by combining the shallow features autonomously selected by the inception structure with the deep features extracted from the temporal and spatial domains. Ultimately, deep features and co-selected features are fused. Our model MCMFuse was tested on the DEAP dataset with cross-validation, showing promising results in emotion recognition.

articleTitle: High-Speed Trajectory Tracking Control for Quadrotors via Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper presents a learning-based high-speed trajectory tracking control strategy for quadrotors, which achieves efficient learning and strong reliability by the collaboration of deep reinforcement learning (RL) and self-tuning mechanism. Different from existing methods, the proposed strategy is designed to explore optimal control performance by taking advantage of model-based self-tuning mechanism and deep reinforcement learning. Specifically, the self-tuning guided deep RL scheme is put forward for quadrotors, with superior learning efficiency and strong adaptability. Firstly, a novel self-tuning mechanism is constructed and some auxiliary variables are introduced to enhance the tracking performance. Then, based on the model-driven self-tuning design, the deep RL is proposed to achieve model-guided learning, where the tuning actions are adopted in the evaluation process during training, aiming at removing the bad explorations by the carefully designed parallel evaluation. Finally, the convergence is analyzed based on the proposed learning framework, which indicates the efficient cooperation of exploration and self-tuning mechanism. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed controller, the guided training and hardware experiments are implemented to show efficient cooperation and satisfactory high-speed trajectory tracking control of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Event-based Adaptive Neural Network Tracking Control Of Uncertain Nonlinear Systems With Unknown Disturbance And Input Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, we delve into the analysis of a specific category of constrained nonlinear systems exhibiting strict feedback, incorporating input time delay as well as time-varying perturbations. We introduce an adaptive control strategy utilizing event-triggered neural networks, complemented by a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) aimed at estimating the unknown composite disturbance, encompassing external perturbations and approximation errors. The approximation of the unknown nonlinear functions is achieved through radial basis functions neural networks (RBFNN). To address the challenges posed by input time delay, we employ the Padé approximation for effective compensation. To address the state constraint problem, we employ the Barrier Lyapunov function (BLF). Leveraging the Lyapunov stability theory, we demonstrate that all signals within the closed-loop system are ultimately semi-globally consistent ultimately bounded (SGUUB). Furthermore, the analysis reveals minimal tracking error between the system’s output and the reference signal. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Data-driven virtual inertia LQR control for new energy systems
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In order to improve the inertia support capability of new energy grid connected inverters for power systems, this paper mainly studies the design problem of an optimal quadratic regulation control algorithm based on the virtual inertia of DC capacitor energy. Based on the typical topology of new energy grid connected inverters, the dynamic foundation of virtual synchronous machines was quantitatively analyzed. On the basis of analyzing the dynamic characteristics, we further quantitatively obtained the mathematical relationship between inertia parameters and system frequency response characteristic s. When considering load changes, the system frequency changes, which can lead to the charging and discharging process of DC capacitors. By designing a virtual inertia controller, the energy of the DC capacitor can be further released, providing inertia support for the system. It is worth noting that the design of the LQR control algorithm in this article is different from the traditional control algorithm design framework based on the Riccati equation. This article mainly proposes a data-driven LQR control algorithm design method. The algorithm design framework can be independent of system model parameters, and based on the input/output data of the system. The least squares method can be used to learn the optimal controller parameters through iterative algorithm design. In the simulation experiment section at the end of the paper, the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed controller design method were verified.

articleTitle: Meticulous prediction of vacuum contactor fault with denoising and decomposition based temporal model
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Vacuum contactor is a crucial electrical component for power conversion and distribution, and thus its safe performance is paramount in practical industry. Its fault prediction helps to avoid serious accidents. The complete operational cycle of a vacuum contactor generally consists of two stages, namely closing and opening. Most published researches detect faults of vacuum contactor after the whole opening and closing stages, making it challenging to forecast faults before the contactor opens. To address this issue, the present paper proposes a meticulous fault prediction method of vacuum contactor with denoising and decomposition based temporal model. The original current signal is denoised and decomposed to obtain the filtered signal components, which are input to corresponding serial models separately. Therefore, the current components for opening stage can be predicted at the closing stage. The predicted components are further reconstructed for fault prediction. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves a higher fault recognition rate over related approaches, demonstrating its considerable practical value.

articleTitle: Airfoil Design and Performance Optimization of Rotorcraft Robots through the Integration of LSTM-PSO and Multilayer Perceptron Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This study designs and employs the Long Short-Term Memory-Particle Swarm Optimization (LSTM-PSO) algorithm, supplemented by a multilayer perceptron model, focusing on the optimization of rotorcraft airfoil structural parameters in low Reynolds number environments under Mars’s unique atmospheric conditions. A new airfoil was successfully developed through the optimized structure. The advantage of this algorithm lies in significantly enhancing the lift-to-drag ratio under ultra-low Reynolds number conditions and achieving a significant reduction in computation time by using a multilayer perceptron to replace traditional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. This strategy not only reflects an effective improvement over traditional design methods but also demonstrates the tremendous potential of using machine learning technologies to handle complex optimization problems in the aerospace field, offering new insights for finding complex optimization solutions in dynamic and uncertain environments.

articleTitle: CDT-YOLO: A Long-term Detection and Tracking Algorithm for Infrared Moving Small Objects in Missile-Borne Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: To improve the accuracy and speed of missile detection and tracking for infrared moving small objects (IMSO), a continuous detection and tracking algorithm called CDT-YOLO is proposed. The algorithm mainly consists of an object detection module based on an improved YOLOv8, a tracking confidence evaluation module, and a multi-scale tracking module based on template matching. The object detection module has demonstrated excellent detection performance for IMSO in complex backgrounds. The YOLOv8 model introduces a lightweight convolution known as GSConv to balance detection accuracy and speed. Additionally, the model uses Wise-IoU (WIoU) v3 as a bounding box regression loss to improve localization ability. The object tracking module shows high robustness to size transformation and rapid movement of small objects. The tracking confidence evaluation module is able to re-invoke the detection algorithm to resume tracking the object when the tracking status is found to be abnormal. After experimental validation, the inference speed of the object detection algorithm exceeds 134 FPS with precision up to 0.842 and AP50 up to 0.692. The CDT-YOLO algorithm outperforms classic tracking algorithms in terms of tracking success rate (Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>) up to 0.774 and speed more than 290 FPS. The method also has the capability of long-term tracking and can be operated in real-time on the missile platform.

Author Keywords: infrared moving small object detection and tracking

articleTitle: A Morphing Quadrotor with Transformable Arms: Modelling, Control and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: A novel morphing quadrotor (MQ) that can adapt to variable task and environment is proposed in this paper. The MQ includes two deformable multi-link support arms that can alter its shape to cross narrow spaces, which increases the versatility of quadrotors. A dynamic model of the MQ is constructed by the Newton-Euler approach, which involves the dynamic of two morphing support arms that will not appear in the conventional multi-rotor UAVs with fixed geometry. Based on the dynamic model, a nonlinear controller is designed to address the attitude stability control of MQ during deformation. Ultimately, the stability of the proposed attitude controller is proved through the Lyapunov method, and numerical simulation tests are performed to validate the effectiveness of the developed MQ system.

articleTitle: Research on Semantic Description Algorithm for Dual-Feature Fusion Images Based on Transformer Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In the method of feature extraction for images, regional feature extraction and grid feature extraction have their own advantages and disadvantages, and a single feature extraction leads to incomplete information of the extracted features, as well as the feature extraction network can not maximize the preservation of the content and details of the original image, etc., a dual-feature fusion Transformer network is proposed to achieve the complementary advantages of the two features. The method first uses ViT grid feature extraction as the main feature extraction method in the feature extraction stage, by segmenting the input image into grid blocks and learning the feature vectors of each grid block using the Transformer encoder to capture the overall semantic information of the image, and in order to make up for the insufficiency of the ViT in dealing with the local detail information, Oscar region feature extraction is introduced as the auxiliary input for extracting local features in the image, followed by the use of Meshed Decoder decoding strategy in the decoding process, i.e., combining different levels of feature mapping into a triangular dissected grid to better utilize the spatial context information for reconstruction. Experimental comparisons are made on the MS COCO benchmark dataset and the effectiveness of the model is verified through quantitative evaluation and qualitative analysis, which show that the method can enhance the dependence on visual information and make the generated descriptive statements more accurate and detailed.

articleTitle: Co-design of adaptive polynomial event-triggered scheme and polynomial fuzzy fault detection filter for polynomial fuzzy systems
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: For networked polynomial fuzzy systems (PFSs), the co-design of the adaptive polynomial event-triggered scheme (APETS) and the fault detection scheme is investigated in this paper. The novel APETS is adopted to reduce the burden of communication where the singularity problem of the adaptive threshold is avoided and the design freedom is enhanced through polynomial weight matrices. Considering the unmatched premise variables (PVs) caused by APETS and the transmission delay, asynchronous filters are established while different membership functions (MFs) and the fuzzy rule numbers (FRNs) from the original system are utilized for more flexible filters. In the solution process, considering the specificity of the form of the stability analysis constraints, local stability is discussed by a permutationbased approach. Finally, two simulation examples are adopted to verify the feasibility and efficacy of the posed method in terms of reducing conservativeness, improving design flexibility and fault detection performance, and the effect of the filter matrix order is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Improving Deep Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Rewards via Self-Imitation Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) often employs intrinsic rewards to promote effective exploration in sparse reward environments. However, the coefficients for these intrinsic rewards are typically set to a uniform value throughout the learning process. This practice negatively impacts the performance of the deep RL agent by limiting its adaptability to environmental complexities, thereby affecting the balance between exploration and exploitation. Self-imitation learning (SIL) can mitigate this negative impact by selectively replicating successful past experiences. However, it also disrupts the learning of the deep RL agent using intrinsic rewards, thereby affecting the agent's performance. To prevent SIL from disrupting the learning of the deep RL agent employing intrinsic rewards and to enhance the performance of the agent, we propose Intrinsic Rewards-Based Self-Imitation Learning (IRSIL) for the on-policy actor-critic deep RL method that utilizes intrinsic rewards. Unlike traditional SIL, IRSIL allows the actor-critic deep RL agent employing intrinsic rewards to only imitate past experiences that facilitate the agent in learning optimal behaviors without disrupting the agent's learning. Specifically, IRSIL stores episodes yielding positive extrinsic rewards into the experience replay buffer. It then makes the actor-critic deep RL agent imitate state-action pairs from this replay buffer exclusively when their extrinsic returns exceed the agent's current value estimates, which are estimated based on both extrinsic and intrinsic rewards. These experimental results in sparse reward procedurally generated MiniGrid environments demonstrate our approach IRSIL significantly enhances the learning and performance of the actor-critic deep RL agent utilizing intrinsic rewards. Furthermore, IRSIL surpasses the performance of both traditional and state-of-the-art SIL approaches in these settings.

articleTitle: StackedFormer: A 1D-transformer model for bearing fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Given the variability and complexity of fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, traditional convolutional architectures exhibit deficiencies in feature representation, leading to suboptimal fault identification rates that fail to fully reflect the operational state of the machinery. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel one-dimensional Transformer model for fault diagnosis—StackedFormer (SF). Firstly, we refine the computation of self-attention within the traditional Transformer framework. Subsequently, the StackedFormer Block (SFB) is employed to incrementally extract features from the raw vibration signals. Finally, the efficacy of our approach is validated using bearing datasets from the University of Paderborn in Germany and Case Western Reserve University. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to other methodologies, our novel approach achieves higher fault diagnosis accuracy and superior performance in fault identification.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Dual Graph Neural Network for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction has become a crucial task in the field of autonomous driving. To improve the accuracy of pedestrian trajectory prediction, researchers primarily concentrate on tackling two key challenges. One is to extract the intricate interactions between pedestrians, and the other is to simulate the diverse decision-making intentions displayed by pedestrians. However, most existing methods utilize the distance attribute to build the relationship of pedestrians only, but ignore other features such as the steering. Besides, some generation theory based methods would lead to substantial deviations in the generated trajectory distribution since they always refine the variational likelihood lower bound of observed data. In this paper, we adopt Graph theory and propose a Spatial-Temporal Dual Graph neural network for pedestrian trajectory prediction. In the proposed method, we construct a pedestrian graph structure by utilizing pedestrian distance and steering features to extract more comprehensive interaction information. Additionally, we introduces the flow-based Glow-PN module to predict multi-modal trajectories of pedestrians. Experimental results on two public benchmark datasets show that our model achieves superior prediction performance and operates effectively in diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: State Estimation for Complex Networks with Randomly Varying Topologies and DoS Attacks Under Binary Encoding Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, based on using binary encoding scheme, the state estimation issue is tackled for complex networks suffering from nonlinearities, stochastic inner coupling, randomly varying topologies and randomly occurring denial-of-service (DoS) attack. The binary encoding scheme is selected to manage the network communication between the sensor to the estimator. The measurement output is quantized to be encoded into a binary bit string (BBS), the random binary bit flipping is taken into account during the network transmission process caused by channel noise, and the received BBS is decoded by the estimator. The Gaussian-distributed random variables are adopted to reflect the possible stochastic variation of inner coupling strength inside each network node in practice. Three sets of Bernoulli-distributed random variables are put into use to depict the random occurrence of varying topology structures, binary bit flipping and DoS attacks during the network transmission, respectively. Based on the statistical properties analysis of the decoded signal, a equivalent stochastic noise is formulated to reflect the influence of random bit errors. This paper targets the state estimator design in such a situation so that the estimation error system achieves the exponential ultimate boundedness in mean square. Through stochastic analysis and inequality operation, a sufficient condition is brought forward for the presence of the satisfactory exponentially ultimately bounded estimator. The estimator gains are yielded readily through solving the matrix inequalities. Ultimately, a numerical simulation example is carried on to validate the usefulness of the estimation method put forth in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration Method of Multi-source Sensors for Autonomous Vehicles Considering Three-dimensional Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The proliferation of sensors and computer technology accelerates the advancement of autonomous driving technology. Manufacturers are continuously introducing various autonomous driving systems that rely on perception sensors and vehicle computers for environment detection and real-time data processing. In the process of seeking the optimal configuration of multi-source sensors for self-driving cars, this paper proposes a joint optimal configuration scheme of Solid-State (SS) LiDARs and High Definition (HD) cameras based on three-dimensional perception. By analyzing the sensing performance of SS LiDARs and HD cameras, a multi-sensor joint configuration optimization model is established, and through the quantification of the 3D sensing area range, it aims to achieve the goal of maximizing the coverage of the sensing area under the condition of ensuring redundant configuration of critical areas. In this model, the cost and computational resources required for sensors are considered as the key constraints to find the number and the placement of SS LiDARs and HD cameras installed in the optimal configuration. To address this problem, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is selected for model solving and the superiority of the proposed method is verified through comparative simulation experiments. The results are beneficial in providing decision support for the joint optimization design of perception schemes in autonomous vehicles, thereby facilitating the creation of sensor configurations that are both more efficient and more effective.

articleTitle: A Triboelectric Smart Insole for Capturing Complex Stress on Plantar Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are serious concerns for people with diabetes, and more than 15% of diabetes patients are expected to develop a DFU during their lifetime, which creates a significant economic burden and impacts on patients’ quality of life. However, current clinical assessment of DFU risk suffers from subjectivity and delayed detection, lacking early warning and intervention capabilities, thus limiting the effectiveness of treatment. Studies have demonstrated that quantifying compressive and shear stresses within the gait process offers a superior approach for assessing DFU risk. Inconveniently, current gait analysis devices exhibit limitations in terms of comfort, continuous monitoring, privacy concerns, and long-term stability, with a critical absence of shear stress detection capability. In this paper, we introduce a real-time triboelectric smart insole for gait analysis, featuring a triboelectric smart textile array in high-stress foot regions, and a flexible printed circuit (FPC) for signal transmission. The electrical signals, generated during gait movements, are transmitted via stainless steel yarns to the FPC, which subsequently communicates these signals to the users using low-power consumption bluetooth. The device’s fully flexible design enhances comfort and durability for prolonged wear and patients’ gait monitoring. Furthermore, we have successfully integrated an interlocked hill structure, inspired by mammalian skin, into the triboelectric smart textile. This innovation helps focus and amplify localized stress, enabling rapid acquisition of external stimulus information with high sensitivity (0.05V/kPa), fast response time (less than 35ms, comparable to human skin), and accurate sensing of a wide stress range (1-200kPa). The compressive and shear stress cues obtained from the triboelectric smart textile are key parameters for DFU risk assessment, and assisted rehabilitation monitoring, providing a potential solution for low-cost, energy-efficient, and universally applicable smart healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Anti-eavesdropping distributed fusion filtering for multi-rate nonlinear systems with missing measurements*
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel anti-eavesdropping distributed fusion filtering algorithm is proposed for multi-rate nonlinear systems with missing measurements over sensor networks, where the missing measurements are characterized by Bernoulli random variables. During the information exchange of sensor nodes, it is assumed that there exists an eavesdropper. Accordingly, an active contamination strategy is introduced to ensure the confidentiality of information transmission. Meanwhile, a corresponding compensation strategy is adopted in the receiver side in order to reduce the performance loss. The main objective of this paper is to design a distributed filtering algorithm such that an upper bound on the local filtering error covariance is obtained and the filter gain optimizing the upper bound is given accordingly. In addition, the fusion filter is obtained by using the covariance intersection fusion criterion, and the monotonicity is analyzed about the upper bound on the filtering error covariance with respect to the occurrence probability of missing measurements. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through a simulation experiment.

articleTitle: A Gradient-based Topology Design Algorithm Applied to Second-order Network for Pursuing Best Possible Synchronization*
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: As is well-known, synchronization acts as one of the most significant dynamic properties of interaction-induced networks, which is depicted by the ratio of the maximal and the second smallest eigenvalues of topology Laplacian matrix and thus could be optimized by tuning the topology of network. Second-order interactions involving three units have been prevalent to describe some real organization of social, biological systems, etc. correspondingly, pursuing the best possible synchronization of second-order network is converted into an optimization problem of second-order topology design. Although some traditional searching technologies, such as simulated annealing, have been adopted to find a candidate optimal second-order topology, the inherent defection on those algorithms, such as the well-known ease of falling into the slow convergence, limiting their application. In this paper, the gradient of eigenvalues of Laplacian matrix is described by a function of the associated eigenvector and the objective hyperlinks. By utilizing Taylor’s formula, a gradient-based topology optimization algorithm is designed to search for the minimum eigen-ratio to improve second-order network synchronization, which can also be extended to higher-order networks. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed gradient-based method. It is observed that our algorithm could achieve an optimized second-order topology within less time on an order of magnitude compared to simulated annealing and thus can be applied to large-scale networks.

articleTitle: A power density output prediction method for solid oxide fuel cells based on a radial basis function neural network model with a gaussian function variable radius drosophila optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Due to the high operating temperature of the solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and the sealing structure, it is long and difficult to directly measure its operating parameters. Therefore, this study adopts a modeling method based on the radial basis function (RBF) neural network to accurately predict the SOFC system’s output power density. Specifically, firstly, the mechanism modeling method is adopted to model the SOFC system with Aspen Plus software, to collect a large amount of experimental data as the training set and test set of the model. Then, the drosophila optimization algorithm (gaussian Network-based drosophila Optimization Algorithm, GNFOA) based on the gaussian function variable radius is combined with the RBF neural network to optimize the network’s weight and bias to enhance the model’s predictive accuracy. The discoveries indicate that the GNFOA based RBF neural network model shows high precision and dependability when forecasting the SOFC system’s output power density. The R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values of the training set and the test set are greater than 0.98, the value of RMSE is less than 0.22, and the value of MSE is less than 0.05.

articleTitle: Dynamic Output Feedback Control of Networked Systems with Medium Access Constrains
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the dynamic output feedback control problem for a category of networked systems with medium access constraints and stochastic packet dropout. The medium access constraints on the controller-actuator side is governed by a Markov chain, and the packet dropout in the network channel can be described by a Bernoulli distribution process. Then, the networked control system is converted into a Markovian jump system with multiple switching modes. Additionally, the dynamic output feedback control strategy is designed, and sufficient conditions to ensure the robustly stability of the closed-loop networked systems are derived grounded on the Lyapunov stability theory and the LMI technique. Finally, a simulation example is provided to illustrate the correctness as well as the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Covert attack design on UAV formation in dynamic target tracking tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The present paper introduces a covert attack design strategy on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) formation, which is mainly applied to the task of tracking dynamic targets. The covert attacks rely on exploiting cyber vulnerabilities, enabling attackers to manipulate GPS readings and inject false information into UAVs through data links. The tracked target in this attack effectively deceives the onboard Global Positioning System (GPS) sensor readings, Laser Distance Sensor (LDS) readings, and manipulates control inputs without altering the network topology of the UAV swarm, thereby inducing increased formation errors between UAVs. Under these conditions, we initially provide the definition and precondition for covert attacks to exist. Subsequently, by transforming the attack problem into a quadratic programming problem with quadratic constraints, we give a design scheme for covert attacks that maximizes the formation error among UAVs. The effectiveness and practicality of the scheme are demonstrated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Cross-turbine fault diagnosis for wind turbines with SCADA data: A spatio-temporal graph network with multi-task learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) data based fault diagnosis for wind turbines is gaining attention due to its accessibility and affordability. However, existing deep learning methods struggle to effectively model SCADA data because of its complex spatio-temporal correlations. In addition, both the variability among wind turbines and the poor generalization of models make it difficult to port the trained model with existing data to others. To tackle these issues, a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network with multi-task learning named MTSTGCN has been proposed for cross-turbine fault diagnosis. MTSTGCN includes a graph data construction module, a graph learning module to learn spatio-temporal features, a domain adaptive module to learn invariant features for different turbine domains and a deep metric learning module for feature discrimination enhancement. The model is trained end-to-end, enabling collaborative multi-task training. The results of experiments conducted on two SCADA datasets indicate that the proposed method outperforms other baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Two distributed singleton formation avoidance strategies for noncooperative target fencing
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The cooperative fencing control problem has been extensively studied mainly in the context of multiple pursuers, also called agents, and one single evader usually called the target. The most popular scenario in the literature is, that the pursuers move in a circular formation to encircle and track the target. The requirement of the circular formation imposes a heavy burden on the distributed coordination among the pursuers. Fortunately, a novel cooperative fencing control framework proposed in [1] only drives the pursuers to form an arbitrary convex hull that could change over time. However, this cooperative fencing control framework also has a drawback in that, the collinear singleton formation could happen and result in ineffective fencing. In [1], a centralized singleton formation avoidance strategy requires that the target information is known to all pursuers. Besides, it fails in more complex settings, for example, the noncooperative target case. By means of a novel rotational term, this paper improves the singleton formation avoidance strategy in [1]. First, we trim the original rotational term and drive only two pursuers to break the singleton formation. Meanwhile, we use only distances between neighboring pursuers to impose additional restrictions on the collision avoidance function, which turns out to be fully distributed. Moreover, the target studied here is noncooperative under a bounded unknown velocity input. The novel strategies together with the nonsmooth cooperative fencing control algorithm are supported by rigorous theoretical analysis. Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our novel design.

articleTitle: Trajectory-user linking via Complexed-Valued Multi-Layer Perception with Fast Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The Trajectory-User Linking (TUL) task has gained increasing importance as it enables providers to establish connections between diverse online identifiers, ultimately enhancing user profiling and overall experience. Despite the increasing importance of this task, traditional machine learning methods based on statistical analysis lack the capability to capture the inherent interactions within time series and analyze their superior characteristics of a global view and energy compaction. Meanwhile, prevailing deep learning methodologies often tend to be intricate, imposing substantial computational burdens during model training. To address this challenge, the Complex-Valued Multi-Layer Perception with Fast Fourier Transform (CVMLP-FFT) is proposed, which extends traditional MLP to complex space to form complex-valued MLP, and designs two transformation modules on the channel and temporal features. The Channel Transformation Module facilitates communication across distinct channels, functioning on each timestamp by employing shared weights among segments to discern channel dependencies. Simultaneously, the Temporal Transformation Module focuses on learning temporal patterns in the frequency domain. Constructed with shared weights between channels, it also extracts temporal features. These temporal features are subsequently fed into a Softmax module for user identification, thereby recognizing and generating trajectories associated with specific users. Compared with baselines in a real-world user trajectory dataset, the proposed method achieves a notable 5.49% improvement in ACC. The CVMLP-FFT significantly reduces the computational burden, providing a more efficient solution for Trajectory-User Linking classification tasks.

Author Keywords: Complex-Valued Multi-Layer Perception with Fast Fourier Transform

articleTitle: An Adaptive Dynamic Migration-based Constrained Multiobjective State Transition Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Complex constrained multi-objective optimization problems are often characterized by narrow and disconnected feasible regions, making it challenging to obtain the optimal constrained Pareto front. To improve feasibility, diversity, and convergence in the optimization process, this paper introduces an adaptive dynamic migration-based constrained multi-objective state transition algorithm. The approach starts with an individual-based state transition algorithm, which searches for candidate solutions across the entire search space. Subsequently, these candidate solutions are evaluated using an adaptive dynamic migration constraint handling technique, which enhances the convergence of candidate solutions in the early stages of optimization and ensures their feasibility in the later stages. The migration process is adaptively adjusted based on the diversity and convergence of the population to maintain a balance among feasibility, diversity, and convergence. Experiments conducted on 14 benchmark problems reveal that the proposed method demonstrates superior or, at the very least, competitive performance when compared to other well-established methods.

articleTitle: Sub-Module Capacitor Voltage Balancing Control Based on Model Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Sub-module (SM) capacitor voltage unbalance is a significant attention in Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC). The complexity of capacitor voltage balancing control closely depends on the number of SMs. This paper analyzes the factors of SM capacitor voltage unbalance, identifies the drawbacks of traditional capacitor voltage balancing control, and proposes a model prediction method for SM capacitor voltage balance control. The SM capacitor voltage and arm current are estimated in real-time based on and utilizing their variation patterns. The deviation of the SM capacitor output voltage from the actual to the theoretical value is measured, and the voltage deviation compensation value is estimated. A neuro-network is used to predicate the SM switching order and accomplish the control. By doing so, the capacitor voltage balancing control is much faster and the capacitor voltage offset is reduced while satisfying the accuracy. In order to validate the practicability of the proposed scheme, an MMC model is fabricated in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Application of Sensors in Flexible Process Control of Intelligent Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In order to carry out the intelligent production of typical chemical products for the application of order-based flexible production system, based on intelligent measurement and control technology, a new generation of information technology such as industrial Internet, intelligent management and control, data visualization, and informatization is integrated. In this paper, we study the establishment of an order-based flexible production process with definable configuration according to the intelligent processing mode of process automation. After selecting the sensor reasonably, Configuration of the industrial intelligent detection system, System signal processing and digitalization, Industrial information network construction and debugging, Programming operation and debugging of intelligent measurement and control systems, Production tasks such as visualization and remote monitoring of the production process. The study found,The sensor plays a vital role in the control system control of the DCS -based controller, Liquid level sensors and flow/weight sensors and other key sensors can monitor various parameters in the production process in real time, provide accurate data support for the control system to ensure the accuracy and stability of the ingredient system. And realize the flexible ingredients controlled by program control, and then make the feeding at the same time to improve production efficiency. This research provides a strong technical guarantee for actual production, and provides a feasible implementation method for our intelligent manufacturing process industrial control.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised graphical autoencoder regression modeling for soft sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: For soft sensor in chemical processes, process variables are usually measured at a higher frequency while quality variables are often measured at a lower rate. This discrepancy in measurement frequencies results in a large number of unlabeled data points. In addition, there are instances where the daily recorded component variables are more readily available, contrasting with the difficulty in obtaining data for the quality variable data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel semi-supervised learning framework, TGAE-STN(Transfer entropy based Graph Autoencoder-Spatiotemporal Networks), which employs an encoder-decoder architecture to efficiently handle both unlabeled and labeled data. For unlabeled data, transfer entropy is computed from the original sampling data to facilitate the conversion into graph data and subsequent reconstruction of graph structure. For labeled data, the latent variable obtained from the reconstruction process of the codec is used as the input to the prediction model, and the adjacency matrix is dynamically constructed during the training process. The prediction network uses a spatiotemporal graph model to extract features across both temporal and spatial dimensions. Moreover, the encoder part is updated asynchronously based on the performance of the decoder and the prediction network, facilitating effective utilization of the information from both unlabeled and labeled data. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through a numerical case and a chemical process. The results show that the proposed TGAE-STN method provides a promising solution for soft sensor technology under semi-supervised conditions.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Economic Dispatch of Combined Wind-Photovoltaic-CSP-Fire System Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: By introducing demand response and carbon trading mechanisms, load-side resources can be optimized, linking power generation and consumption to achieve synergistic optimal scheduling in a multi-source joint system. This ensures "peak shaving and valley filling" on the load side while satisfying users’ electricity needs, reducing the regulatory pressure on generation units, and improving the overall economic efficiency of system operations. Carbon trading increases the output costs for traditional thermal power units, enhancing the competitive advantage of wind, photovoltaic, and solar thermal power generation in optimal system scheduling and reducing system CO2 emissions. Considering both demand response and carbon trading costs, a low-carbon economic dispatch model is developed for a wind-photovoltaic-CSP-thermal combined system. This model aims to enhance system operation economy and reduce CO2 emissions. The effectiveness of this proposed model is verified and analyzed through simulations, demonstrating its potential in improving system efficiency and lowering emissions.

articleTitle: Development of a Vision-Based Search System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an autonomous unmanned aircraft system (UAS) that excelled in the Unmanned Platform Stereoscopic Cross-Domain Collaboration Challenge held in Yuxi, China, from August 1-15, 2022. The challenge was divided into four subtasks: (1)navigation and control, (2)recognition and localization, (3)online trajectory planning, and (4)task planning and scheduling, all of which were to be performed autonomously and safely by the robot. To meet these requirements, we designed and implemented a UAS with high autonomy and reliability, built on a hexacopter system, integrating sensors, an onboard computer, power batteries, and an electro-optical pod. We then developed the software algorithm and implemented the executable calculation code, integrated with the UAV hardware system. This paper outlines the main components and design process of the UAS and describes its application in a competition mission.

articleTitle: A Resilient Decentralized Learning Approach against Byzantine Attack via Reputation Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Machine learning is a key component of many applications, among which decentralized learning has attracted wide attention because of its cost-effectiveness and high efficiency. However, decentralized learning is vulnerable to various Byzantine attacks. Existing defense models face challenges in defending against complex attacks and are often constrained by strict network topologies. To address this issue, a parameter aggregation rule based on reputation evaluation (RPV) is proposed in this paper. This rule establishes a reputation model for neighboring nodes and continuously updates it based on their distance performance during each iteration. By applying the reputation model of neighboring nodes to the Beta distribution, their reliability is obtained. Based on the reliability of neighboring nodes, the set of reliable nodes for this iteration and select parameter values from them for aggregation are determined. Finally, we gradually eliminate the influence of Byzantine nodes. Our experimental results on the MNIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is resilient to attacks from any number of Byzantine nodes and outperforms previous defense models in terms of network topology constraints, training accuracy, and computational costs.

articleTitle: Stackelberg Game Theoretical Learning for Multi-Agent Formation Tracking Control
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this article, the formation tracking problem is discussed within a multi-agent framework. Drawing from the hierarchical model featuring a single leader and multiple followers, we use the Stackelberg game to model the system and prove the Stackelberg-Nash equilibrium exists. The solution of the preceding game is resolved by using the deep reinforcement learning algorithm and a generative communication strategy learning algorithm is proposed. The efficacy of the aforementioned methodology is validated through experimental simulations, substantiating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Valve Stiction Quantification Method Based on Deviation Product Analysis and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In response to the widespread issue of valve stiction in process industries, a quantification method based on neural network and deviation product analysis has been proposed. Initially, loop data of varying degrees of stiction, including controller output and process variable, are generated. Through deviation product analysis, dynamic features within the non-stationary time series are extracted. Subsequently, a model capable of accurately identifying the degree of stiction was trained by employing neural network for deep learning on these features, along with a designed loss function that has dynamically adjustable weights. This approach achieved high-precision quantification of valve stiction. Experiments and data analysis have demonstrated the effectiveness of this method in practical industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Forward Obstacle Detection Approach for Trains Based on 4D Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: With the expansion of urban scale, rail transport has become an indispensable component of the city’s public transportation. Achieving intelligent assisted driving in rail transport can reduce incidents due to driver factors. Sensors enabling accurate perception of the surrounding environment are the prerequisite for intelligent assisted driving. 4D Radar generates point clouds that include both 3D position and velocity information. Especially, 4D Radar works well in bad weather conditions compared to Lidar and camera. This paper proposes an obstacle detection method based on 4D Radar in the train-travelling environment, which dynamically adjusts the obstacle detection range using DBSCAN. Moreover, the network is improved for the characteristic of sparse 4D Radar point cloud, and enhancing the detection capability of the network through the introduction of an attention module. Experimental results show that the method achieves satisfactory results in real scenarios and has great potential.

articleTitle: Research on Power System Optimization Algorithm Frameworks Empowered by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing complexity of system structure and refinement of management, power system optimization computation is facing the double pressure of computational accuracy and computational time. Machine learning (ML) techniques can effectively utilize vast historical data to provide new theoretical basis for optimizing stable and fast solutions. This paper is aimed to summarize the optimization algorithm frameworks, which is based on the interaction between ML and optimization computing for general power system optimization problems. The framework empowered by ML mainly includes end-to-end optimization, ML-enhanced optimization, and joint-driven optimization. By utilizing the physical characteristics of power system, these frameworks not only provide a more efficient and reliable calculation scheme for the optimal operation of power system, but also provide innovative solutions for other complex optimization problems.

articleTitle: Output-feedback H∞ Control for Saturated 2-D Discrete System under The Event-triggered Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The output feedback H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control issue is investigated for a class of saturated 2-D discrete systems characterized by the Roesser local state space model within the framework of the static event-triggered mechanism (SETM). Considering the practical issues, such as the system state being challenging to be measured directly or unmeasurable, an event-triggered condition with measurement information is introduced, and the corresponding output feedback controller is constructed. Utilizing the Lyapunov function approach, we ensure that the closed-loop system meets a designated H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance criterion. The index for the output feedback controller are derived through the application of matrix inequalities. Combined with the cone complement linearization (CCL) algorithm. And the development of the output feedback controller is recast as a nonlinear minimization challenge subject to linear matrix inequality constraints. Then, the expected controller gain can be presented. In the end, the proposed output feedback control strategy’s effectiveness and practicality under SETM are validated through a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Stock price prediction based on Weighted Meta-Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: With the continuous development of China's stock market, stock forecasting has gradually become a focus of attention. Aiming at the Meta-ELM algorithm in the field of stock price trend prediction ignores the problem of the existence of the time characteristics in the time series data and the difference in the effect of the base ELM, this paper proposes a short-term stock price trend prediction model based on the Weighted Meta-Extreme Learning Machine (WMeta-ELM). The method first improves the Meta-ELM model by making the number of time steps of the stock data equal to the number of base ELM models, enabling the model to extract time series features from the stock series. In order to better capture the dynamics of the market, the method also introduces a weighting approach that assigns different weights to each base-ELM model to guide the model to learn different information at different time points. In order to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, we compare it with five traditional and advanced models in real stock trading data. The results show that the proposed WMeta-ELM model is more feasible and effective than Meta-ELM.

articleTitle: Adaptive Vector Field Histogram Plus method for local path planning under human—robot collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: As an expanding field that caters to the needs of the elderly and people with disabilities, intelligent wheelchairs aim to enhance the efficiency and safety of individuals with disabilities. Path planning, a pivotal technology under intelligent wheelchair systems, has emerged as a focal point of scholarly exploration. This paper proposes advancements in the vector field histogram plus (VFH+) algorithm, thereby introducing the adaptive VFH+ algorithm (AVFH+). Notably, this paper redefines the calculation of obstacle density and introduces the concept of custom target point density. By dynamically modulating the threshold, we effectively resolve the problems of oscillatory paths during obstacle avoidance, thus averting the predicament of the robot. In addition, the robot's speed is adaptively adjusted based on the opening width, and the trajectory is smoothed using Bezier path planning, enabling the robot to reach the target position through a shorter collision-free and smooth path. The improved AVFH+ algorithm demonstrates excellent path planning capability through multiple simulation experiments in various map environments with different starting points and target locations. The algorithm has the ability to adapt to complex environments, accurately perceive and avoid obstacles, and exhibits significant generalization capabilities. This makes it significant in dense area path planning, providing safer and more efficient mobility solutions in areas such as smart wheelchairs, and actively contributing to the quality of life of people with disabilities. Future research could explore the consideration of dynamic obstacles and validate the performance of the algorithm in real-world environments.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Collaborative Action Decision Mechanism with Mixed Distribution Coefficients for Robotic Grasping
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
