abstract: Robotic arms have high precision, flexibility and automation capabilities, and are widely used in industry, medical and logistics fields. In this paper, we propose a robotic push-grasp collaborative action decision mechanism with mixed distribution coefficients based on reinforcement learning. Two fully convolutional action value functions are designed to perform corresponding pushing and grasping actions, respectively. Each fully convolutional action value function maps visual observations into the best action predictions of the Q-learning algorithm. In order to evaluate the pushing action more comprehensively, a new mixed distribution coefficient measure is proposed to address the distribution of blocks in the scene. The corresponding reward is given depending on whether the pushing action makes the scene more conducive to grasping. In addition, the mixed distribution coefficient measure is introduced into the push-grasp collaborative action decision mechanism. It can optimize the learning network training process, thereby the robot arm can make the most beneficial grasping and pushing action decision based on the real-time training results. Experimental results show that the proposed method has better performance for robotic grasping in complex scenes.

articleTitle: MHNNSL: EEG-Based Emotion Recognized by Multi-task Hypergraph Neural Network combined with Self-supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In recent years, the use of electroencephalography (EEG) for emotion recognition has attracted widespread attention in the fields of human-computer interaction and cognitive science. However, how to establish a brain network model to simulate the dynamic processes of the brain during various cognitive activities, thereby revealing the complex interrelationships between brain regions and completing emotion recognition tasks has become a focus of attention. This paper proposes an EEG emotion recognition model based on Multi-task Hypergraph Neural Network combined with Self-supervised Learning (MHNNSL). Firstly, we perform a hypergraph modeling of the brain network according to the structure of brain regions. Then we use a hypergraph neural network to learn the corresponding features. Moreover, by integrating multiple self-supervised tasks (including spatial transformation task, frequency transformation task, and contrastive learning task), more general representations are learned. Finally, emotion recognition is achieved through a multi-layer perceptron (MLP). To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, comparative experiments were conducted on the publicly available SEED dataset with existing methods. Our proposed model achieved the highest accuracy of 85.17% and successfully reflected the response level of various brain regions to emotional tasks. Meanwhile, ablation experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control for Path-Tracking of Unmanned Agricultural Vehicles with Prescribed Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This article presents a sliding mode control method for path-tracking of unmanned agricultural vehicles (UAV) in unstructured environments. Before the path-tracking errors converge, a prescribed performance control (PPC) protocol is proposed to ensure that the preview errors are kept within predefined boundaries. By combining sliding mode feedback control and PPC, a modified path-tracking controller is then designed to ensure path-tracking control accuracy. Finally, a high-fidelity vehicle model is established for comparative simulations, which verify the superiority of the designed path-tracking controller.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Fault-Tolerant Control for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) subject to possible multiple actuator failures, which is a tough problem to solve with traditional FTC methods since they usually require accurate mathematical models. To address the limitation of traditional FTC methods, a model-free FTC approach is proposed based on reinforcement learning (RL). Subsequently, the proposed approach is applied to construct fault-tolerant controller for UAVs without any knowledge of the quadrotor dynamic information. Then, an end-to-end control policy that can tolerant actuator failures is obtained, which can map the state of the UAVs directly to the control commands of the four rotors after learning. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed fault-tolerant approach is demonstrated by using the flexible modular quadrotor simulator.

articleTitle: GNSS Signal Authentication Method Based on Power Monitoring and Early-late Phase Metric
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signal amplitude is extremely weak through the atmosphere to the ground. Accurate interference detection is an urgent issue to avoid the influence of a wide range of jamming in the complex electromagnetic environment. In the state-of-art interference identification methods, the low reliability of deception interference is the most intractable problem, which seriously affect the classification performance of other interferences. In order to solve this problem, a GNSS signal authentication method is proposed in this paper based on power monitoring and early-late phase (ELP) metric. Under the Bayesian framework, this method utilizes hypothesis testing and simultaneously monitors the received power and the early-late phase metric to achieve effective classification of interference sources in the received signal and improve the reliability of deception interference classification. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method has high reliability for interference detection and classification, particular for the spoofing detection. At the same time, the feasibility of the algorithm is verified through experiments with actual data.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling Methods for General Characteristics of Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: As a complex system that integrates computer science, network communication, and physical processes, it has shown huge potential in many fields. To effectively design, analyze and optimize CPS (Cyber-Physical Systems), establishing appropriate unified methods for modeling, simulation, and analysis of CPS is of crucial importance. In this paper, the concepts and characteristics of CPS are introduced, emphasizing the nature of its interdisciplinary and heterogeneous, as well as the extensive application of aviation, aerospace, vehicle, and other fields. And then existing CPS modeling methods are systematically reviewed and summarized from three perspectives: discrete modeling, continuous modeling, and advanced language modeling methods. The challenges and technical difficulties in CPS modeling process are identified, and three feasible solutions are proposed. The proposed solutions could contribute to the further study of CPS modeling.

articleTitle: Effect of hemiplegia on gait symmetry, complexity and variability during lower limb movements
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The effect of hemiplegia on the kinematic characteristics of the hip, knee, and ankle joints during the gait cycle was explored in detail in this study by comparing and analyzing the changes in the lower limb joint angles in hemiplegic patients with those in the healthy population. Through quantitative methods, it was found that the peak angle of hip joints in hemiplegic patients was asymmetrical, and the peak angle of the healthy side of patients was generally larger than that of the affected side. Especially in the knee joint, the patients' peak angles were not only lower but also reached their peaks earlier than those of healthy individuals, a phenomenon that may be due to compensatory movement strategies resulting from weakened muscle strength on the affected side. Further analysis of gait symmetry showed that the greatest asymmetry of gait in hemiplegic patients occurred at the end of the swing phase of hip, knee, and ankle movements. In addition, joint motion variability and complexity in hemiplegic patients differed significantly from that of the healthy population. These findings have important implications for the development of accurate hemiplegic rehabilitation assessment tools and targeted treatment programs.

articleTitle: Direct Sparse Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry With Covisibility Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a direct sparse monocular visual-inertial odometry system, which based on two techniques called adaptive direct motion refinement and photometric inertial bundle adjustment. To ensure efficient system launch in various scenarios, we design a novel multi-stage initialization strategy based on direct method. The sparse image alignment algorithm fail in cases of severe motion and large light variations. Therefore, we present adaptive direct motion refinement, which ensures robust tracking by dynamically adjusting the inertial residual scale. Although photometric bundle adjustment is efficient for estimating trajectory, there is still a relatively large accumulated error. To further reduce accumulated errors, we propose using photometric inertial bundle adjustment to improve trajectory estimation accuracy. This is achieved by constructing accurate covisibility relations and effectively combining inertial constraints. The performance of proposed method was evaluated on the EuRoC dataset, and the results demonstrate that the trajectory estimation accuracy outperforms existing methods.

articleTitle: Enhanced Session-Based Recommendation Using Multi-Channel Hypergraph Network
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In today’s digital landscape, the drive for supremely personalized content made Session-Based Recommendation (SBR) systems crucial. Traditional methods often overlook the complex high-order relationships among items during the recommendation process. Our paper introduces a Multi-Channel Hypergraph Convolutional Network to enhance SBR systems by addressing these gaps. Our framework first transforms session data into a hypergraph, facilitating many-to-many relationship modeling between items, beyond linear and pairwise associations. It employs hypergraph convolutional layers and a line graph channel to process these intricate relationships and capture inter-session connections. Additionally, it utilizes multi-channel convolution operations with both parallel and serial channels, varying kernel sizes, and filters designed to thoroughly process the encoded multidimensional data to extract essential features. To combat data sparsity, we apply self-supervised learning techniques to maximize mutual information between the learned session representations. This approach significantly improves the system’s accuracy and context-aware recommendations, as demonstrated by our model’s performance improvements on various datasets, including a precision at 10 (P@10) of 40.22% and a mean reciprocal rank at 20 (M@20) of 19.45% on the Diginetica dataset, reflecting substantial advancements over existing models.

articleTitle: Dimensionality Reduction Method for Output Regulation of probabilistic Boolean Control Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, we study the output regulation problem (ORP) of probabilistic Boolean control networks (PBCNs) via event-triggered control. Firstly, the algebraic forms of a PBCN and a reference BN are established via the semi-tentor product. By analyzing the set stabilization of the small auxiliary system and the PBCN, a necessary and sufficient condition to detect the solvability of the ORP is presented. Secondly, a method to design the state feedback event-triggered control for the ORP is proposed. Finally, an example is given to is given to verify the effectiveness of the new results.

articleTitle: Fixed-time synchronization of delayed multiplex networks with impulsive effects
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The fixed-time synchronization of delayed multiplex networks with impulsive effects is studied. The delayed topology of a multiplex network is considered, which contains both interlayer and intra-layer relationships. We thoroughly investigate two distinct impulses, involving synchronizing and desynchronizing impulses, respectively. Besides, we design the adaptive controller to drive the given networks with distinct impulsive effects into fixed-time synchronization. Emphatically, the designed controller has no bearing on any sign functions, and as a result, it eliminates the chattering phenomena that appear in many results from previous research. In addition, sufficient conditions to reach fixed-time synchronization are given under synchronizing and desynchronizing impulses correspondingly. Ultimately, coupled single-link robot arms are chosen as the application of our theoretical findings, and a few illustrative examples are exhibited to present the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Consensus for Multiple Mechanical Systems With Actuator Faults and Dead-Zone Input
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper addresses the finite-time consensus problem in multiple mechanical systems affected by external disturbances, dead-zone input, and actuator faults. Initially, we introduce a linear time-varying model to manage the challenges posed by the interaction between dead-zone input and actuator faults. Building on this foundation, we propose a finite-time consensus algorithm that incorporates the technique of adding a power integrator. Our presented consensus control strategy enables flexible adjustment of actuator faults and dead-zone parameters based on system performance. Through rigorous theoretical analysis, we demonstrate that the consensus tracking errors can converge to a small bounded region around equilibrium point within a finite time. Finally, simulation results are carried out to validate the efficacy of the designed methodology.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Optimization Algorithm Based on Self-organizing Evolutionary Game Model
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Hierarchical optimization is utilized to address problems with varying levels of priority among decision makers. It has wide applications in supply chain management, resource allocation optimization, hierarchical production operations, and other domains. To accommodate the vast array of structures encountered in hierarchical optimization problems, this study introduces an innovative optimization framework based on self-organizing evolutionary game models. Initially drawing inspiration from the Nash game and the Stackelberg game, the priority relationship in hierarchical optimization problems is translated into the leader-follower relationship in the game model. Subsequently, optimization methods based on the evolutionary algorithm are proposed for both the Nash and Stackelberg games. Finally, a self-organized optimization framework grounded in the game models is presented, which can be extended to hierarchical optimization problems involving more than two layers and multiple decision makers in each layer. This framework enables adaptive adjustments for various types of hierarchical optimization problems. Based on the specific structure of the problem and the proposed framework, corresponding optimization algorithms can be developed. The experimental results demonstrate that algorithms based on this framework are adept at solving a wide range of hierarchical optimization problems and consistently yield satisfactory equilibrium solutions.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Kalman Filter Fusion for Multi-sensor System
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop a robust module through the integration of distributionally robust Kalman filter with multi-sensor fusion. Leveraging the established reliability of the robust Kalman filter operating at a single station, we propose its extension to a multi-sensor distributed system, observing a reduction in error resulting from the integrated data fusion across multiple sensors. By employing a target tracking example, we demonstrate the superior performance of our bi-causal optimal transport fusion framework.

articleTitle: Research on the volume measurement algorithm and application of irregular objects based on3D point cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of 3D laser scanning technology, it has provided the basis for the wide application of irregular object volume measurement based on point cloud. However, in practice, how to measure the volume of irregular objects in a single viewing Angle, the existing methods still have some limitations, such as overfitting the surface of the point cloud, large measurement error of non-convex objects, and non-closed point cloud can not be measured. In this paper, a method of measuring the volume of irregular objects in single view based on 3D point cloud is proposed. Firstly, an infrared camera is used to capture the point cloud image of the object at the overlooking Angle, and the spatial position correction is carried out on the point cloud image to make the carrying object plane coincide with the XOY plane. Secondly, the point cloud data unrelated to the measured object is removed, and the object point cloud is projected vertically down to the XOY plane, and the projected area of the point cloud is calculated using regression model and grid method. Finally, the measured object is regarded as a combination of multiple columns with the same base area, and the exact volume of the object is calculated by the accumulation method. Experimental results show that the volume measurement of irregular objects can be completed by using the method proposed in this paper under a single view Angle, and the average relative error rate is only 3.52%.

articleTitle: Human behavior recognition algorithm based on improved 3D ResNet and GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that traditional CNN lacks feature extraction for the time dimension, and the traditional RNN is easy to ignore local information when processing long sequences. In this paper, we propose a spatiotemporal feature extraction network (3D ResNet-Double Gated Recurrent Unit-Convolutional Block Attention Module, RDCnet) fused with convolutional attention mechanism, which first uses the improved 3D ResNet to extract the preliminary spatiotemporal features, and then sends the DGRU module with GRU as the basic unit constructed in this paper to further model the temporal information of the behavior. In this process, the convolutional attention module is introduced to capture the channel correlation and spatial correlation of the behavior. Finally, the classification results are obtained through the softmax layer. The proposed method is evaluated on the publicly available datasets UCF101 and HMDB51. Experimental results show that the average accuracy of the proposed method on the two datasets is 91.3% and 63.4%, and the recognition performance is high.

articleTitle: Cooperative Guidance Method for Multiple Loitering Munitions Based on Track Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: A cooperative guidance method using mid-course guidance trajectory planning is proposed for the long-range precision strike of a small communication-based loitering munition swarm. This method ensures the relative position and states consistency among the loitering munitions before entering a terminal guidance attack. Through the use of a data link for inter-munition communication, coordinated trajectories are planned for each roaming projectile. The consistency in relative position and flight status is improved by employing airspeed control, thereby enhancing the cooperative guidance accuracy. Subsequently, cooperative terminal guidance is achieved by employing an improved proportional navigation law based on segmented guidance. This approach reduces the difficulty of inter-projectile communication while maintaining guidance accuracy, thereby lowering the complexity of terminal guidance laws. Finally, hardware-in-loop simulation and flight tests are conducted for the omnidirectional attack scenario against stationary targets to validate the rationality and effectiveness of this cooperative guidance method.

articleTitle: Multi-robot flocking path planning based on fusion of APF and Improved DWA algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Robot f1ocking systems in unknown environments have higher adaptability, higher efficiency and stronger robustness compared to single robots. In this paper, a control algorithm based on the fusion of the artificial potential field algorithm and the improved dynamic window algorithm is proposed for the path planning in the multi-robot flocking control process. In the free space, the multi-robot flocking will obtain the velocity control input based on the artificial potential field algorithm, and go to the target point quickly with the "quasi-lattice" formation structure; when the robots senses obstacles, control algorithm switches to the dynamic window algorithm, and obtains the control input that can maintain the flocking state and realize the obstacle avoidance at the same time, according to the evaluation function. In this paper, the orientation evaluation function is improved, and a new evaluation functions are added to form an evaluation function with four evaluation indexes, which solves the robot local optimization problem and ensures the formation state of the robots, and improves the excellent trajectory score. The validity and advantages of the proposed algorithm are verified through theoretical analysis and simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Network Attack Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This study aims to address the detection challenges of multiple types of attacks in the field of network security. Traditional statistical-based detection mechanisms struggle to effectively identify and differentiate different types of network attacks. Therefore, we propose a detection system composed of a data preprocessing module and a machine learning-based classification module. In the data preprocessing aspect, we introduce a supplementary method. This method selects appropriate features based on correlation coefficients, reducing the dimensionality of the feature set and improving the performance of the classification model. Through the methods proposed in this study, we can better understand and handle network attacks, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of the detection system.

articleTitle: Reachable-Set-Based Fault Detection for Switched Delayed Systems With Deception Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper investigates the fault detection problem of a class of switched delayed systems (SDSs) affected by deception attacks. Utilizing the framework of output reachable set theory, a fault detection methodology reliant on reachable set is established to effectively tackle the fault detection challenge in the presence of bounded peak interference inputs, fault signals, and attack signals. By jointly constructing the combined switching strategy and time-dependent multiple Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (TMLF), sufficient conditions are derived for the design of fault detection filter (FDF), and the corresponding logic relationship for fault detection is developed. Ultimately, an example is ultimately presented to corroborate the efficacy of the obtained findings.

articleTitle: Classified Event-Triggered Mechanism for Networked Switched Systems Under Integrity Deception Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper proposes an event-triggered secure output regulation (SOR) control strategy against integrity deception attacks (IDAs) for networked switched systems (NSSs) with frequency-limited persistent dwell time (FPDT). Switching law based on FPDT allows for a much larger number of activated unstable subsystems than activated stable subsystems and all switching instants of subsystems and subcontrollers to be unstable. IDAs not only deceive input and output signals, but also tamper with switching signals. From the perspective of communication, cyclic redundancy check (CRC) technology is applied to detect IDAs in bilateral channel networks. The classified event-triggered mechanism (CETM) provides trigger conditions for input signal, output signals and switching signal separately. Compared to single ETMs where the switching signal and the output signal share the same triggering condition, CETM reduces the frequency of switching signal being attacked, thereby shortening asynchronous duration. Finally, a model of areo-engine is used to validate the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Study on the Market Response Strategy of MultiType Load Participation in Peaking Auxiliary Service with Load Side Counting and Customer’s Willingness
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Against the background of the gradual exhaustion of deep regulation space on the power side, there is an urgent need to actively tap the existing flexible regulation potential on the load side and utilize market-based incentives to realize the aggregated utilization of flexible regulation resources on the load side. In this paper, the customer willingness coefficient is quoted to characterize the change of the customer’s electricity consumption with the electricity price, and a market response model for multi-type loads to participate in the peaking auxiliary service is established, according to which, the optimization strategy of the market response model for multitype loads to participate in the peaking auxiliary service is further researched. The analysis of the example shows that the model can effectively improve the load curve and reduce the cost of electricity purchased by users, which verifies the optimization effect of the market response strategy of multi-type load participation in peaking auxiliary services.

articleTitle: Research on Smoke and Fire Target Detection with Tracking Algorithm Based on YOLOv8 and DeepSORT
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In addition to destroying the natural environment and causing loss of private and public property, human-caused and natural fires also greatly endanger public safety. As a result, accurately assessing the fire situation and keeping an eye on it in real time are highly valuable both theoretically and practically. In order to address the shortcomings of earlier methods and raise the model's detection accuracy even more, we proposed a smoke and fire target identification algorithm in this thesis that is based on YOLOv8. Enhancing the C2f module by expanding the algorithm's capacity for feature extraction without adding more model parameters by utilizing deformable convolution in the backbone network; To increase the feature fusion capabilities, the Dynamic Head, a target detection head based on the attention mechanism, replaces the original model's detection head. Furthermore, numerous inanimate items that share similarities with fire and smoke characteristics are wrongly identified in the scene, and there are false alarms and missed alarms in the current studies on fire and smoke recognition. On the other hand, smoke and fire in a fire situation have dynamic characteristics like diffusion and spreadability. Static targets can be recognized as false alarm scenarios, while dynamic targets can be recognized as locations where smoke and fire actually occur. In order to differentiate between dynamic and static targets, the SSIM metric is introduced into the DeepSORT algorithm, which is enhanced based on the target identification algorithm. The enhanced DeepSORT algorithm essentially addresses the issues of false alarms and missed alarms that arise during the detection phase, while the enhanced target identification method raised the average accuracy by 1.5% over the initial YOLOv8 algorithm.

articleTitle: Coupling Analysis and Feedforward Compensation Design of Two-axis Gimbal Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Gimbal systems are pivotal in fields ranging from aerospace to photography, demanding high precision and stability. Traditional pitch-yaw decoupled control strategies ignores the dynamics coupling of the two axes, thus often faltering to meet the stringent requirements for precision and stability. This research dissects the intricate coupling effects between the gimbal axes. By implementing a strategic feedforward compensation channel, the system is reduced to two decoupled double-integrator with minor disturbance terms and further stabilized by two cascade PID controllers. The hidden state used by the compensation term is acquire by our designed Luenberger observer, whose stability is proved to guarantee the correctness of our algorithm. Simulations based on real-world parameters validates the performance of our proposed algorithm and superiority than pure PID. Our methodology not only stabilizes the gimbal with reduced tracking error and quicker response times but also offers a robust framework adaptable to other multi-axis control systems.

articleTitle: Efficient Incremental Adaptation Method for Decision-making Model
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The enhancement of decision-making models is of great significance in augmenting the applicability of unmanned systems in complex scenarios. This paper proposes an incremental adaptation method for local trajectory planning decision-making model. The method establishes a Decision Skills Association Model (DSAM), which associates previously learned decision skills with the current scenario to output suitable objective function parameters. Our method actively generates scenarios for further training according to the DSAM’s condition, efficiently expanding the DSAM. A key information extraction method is also employed to enhance the efficiency of decision skills learning. The experimental results show that our method helps unmanned system to achieve generally favorable performance in various scenarios. Moreover, the active exploration strategy and key information extraction method enhance the learning efficiency of both the DSAM and the decision skills learning model.

articleTitle: An Integrated Model-Driven and Data-Driven Method Based on CFD-PSO-RBF: Applications to Leakage Detection of Natural Gas Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: To address the issues of low accuracy, poor interpretability, and over-reliance on data in conventional model-based and data-based methods for pipeline leakage detection (PLD), an integrated model-driven and data-driven approach is proposed in this paper. In the presented method, the particle swarm optimised radial basis function (PSO-RBF) neural network is introduced into the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of the pipeline. Such the hybrid model improves the accuracy of the pipeline description by employing PSO-RBF to compensate for the errors generated by the model-based approach due to inaccurate meshing and imprecise modeling. The CFD model for the natural gas pipeline is initially built using the Ansys Fluent platform for offline training. It is then integrated with the PSO-RBF model. In the online detection stage, the trained CFD-PSO-RBF model is utilized for online prediction and real-time monitoring of pipeline operation. To demonstrate the application potential of the developed method, it is successfully employed to detect natural gas leakage in a laboratory simulating a real natural gas pipeline. Experimental results show that, in comparison to the traditional methods, the CFD-PSO-RBF method improves the accuracy of leakage detection and performs well in terms of response time.

Author Keywords: particle swarm optimization of radial basis function (PSO-RBF)

articleTitle: Personalized Lane-changing Behavior Decision Model Considering Driving Habits
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The development of automated driving technologies for humans should adopt a human-centered approach to ensure safety and satisfactory user experience. Making automated lane change decisions in high-speed traffic flows is extremely challenging, especially when considering the habits and preferences of different drivers. To address this problem, this paper proposes a personalized lane change behavior decision model considering driving habits. Instead of directly mimicking human behavior, the method employs inverse reinforcement learning to learn the driver-driving behavior generation mechanism from personal historical driving trajectories and select personalization indicators to describe the driver’s preferences in lane-changing decisions. The risk field is invoked to design a reward function to enhance the interpretability of personalized decision-making by portraying the driver’s perception of risk. The model is trained and tested in a multi-lane highway scenario. Results show that the proposed method can make lane-changing decisions, which are consistent with the driver’s driving habits. Additionally, our model analyzes the characterization of relevant indicators that influence lane-changing decisions.

articleTitle: Collaborative Decision-making in Heterogeneous UAV Swarms based on Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Addressing the complexity of collaborative decision-making within heterogeneous UAV swarms in dynamic scenarios, and the difficulty in understanding the overall mission, this paper presents the AM-Qmix algorithm. The algorithm incorporates the prioritized multi-pool of experience replay approach into deep reinforcement learning for heterogeneous multi-agent systems, enhancing the learning capabilities of the UAV swarm. Additionally, through local behavioral guidance strategies, the algorithm improves UAVs' understanding and execution efficiency for specific tasks, thereby increasing the collaborative decision-making capacity of the entire swarm. Simulation experiments conducted on collaborative material transport tasks with heterogeneous UAV swarms have demonstrated the superiority of our algorithm in resolving issues of collaborative decision-making among heterogeneous UAV swarms.

articleTitle: The Propagation Process for Predator-prey Model of Worm in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) serve diverse applications but susceptible to malicious attacks. Limited research has explored the impact of protected nodes on worm propagation within WSNs, considering differential dynamics. Quantitative investigation of WSN worm propagation models, incorporating focused protection, is conducted using the Holling-II class predator-prey model. This work is focused on: 1. Establishing local and global asymptotic stability conditions. 2. Investigating Hopf bifurcation and identifying key parameters. 3. Determining conditions for Hopf bifurcation. 4. Discussing bifurcation direction and periodic solution stability. 5. Deriving parameter thresholds for transitioning from viral to virus-free equilibrium. Based on these findings, a virus prevention and control scheme is designed. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments validate the model’s utility as a reference for network worm prevention and control.

articleTitle: Intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting: An end-to-end Transformer-based network
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The exponential growth of photovoltaic (PV) power generation prompts accurate PV forecasting due to the nature of PV power fluctuations. Cloud movements have a significant impact on solar irradiance, which further affects PV power. Although there are many models available to predict intra-hour irradiance using ground-based sky images, most of them are based on long short term memory (LSTM) and convolution nerual network (CNN) models. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end Transformer-based model, where Informer extracts historical time-series data features and ViViT extracts sequential ground-based sky image features. Finally, the multi-modal features are concatenated in the predictive network and then go through the fully connected layer to forecast intra-hour direct normal irradiance (DNI). Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model has a forecast skill of 35.814%, 30.407%, and 31.492% on 10-minute ahead (MA), 20 MA, and 30 MA, respectively, which outperforms the LSTM model and the CNN model. Moreover, it proves the feasibility and effectiveness of combining time series data with ground-based sky images.

articleTitle: Robust anti-disturbance control of nonlinear systems by a dual-pole assignment based disturbance observer design
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust anti-disturbance control scheme for nonlinear systems subject to time-varying load disturbances. Firstly, a nonlinear generalized proportional-integral observer (NGPIO) is designed to estimate the system state, load disturbance and its high-order derivatives in real time. Different from the existing single-pole assignment based GPIO designs, a dual-pole assignment approach is proposed to determine the NGPIO gain, such that the observer gain responsible for estimating the disturbance dynamics could be specifically tuned with only slightly impact on the observer gain associated with the state estimation. By virtue of the estimated system state and load disturbance, a nonlinear anti-disturbance controller is then designed, followed by robust stability analysis of the resulting closed-loop system. Finally, two illustrative examples are presented to verify the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fusion Estimation for Networked Systems Subject to Transmission Power Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The paper discusses the problem of sequential fusion (SF) state estimation for wireless sensor network systems with transmission power constraints. Limited transmission power in wireless communication networks may have an impact on the effectiveness and stability of information transmission. To address this issue, a recursive SF state estimator is derived based on the sequential order of sensor observations reaching the remote estimator. Simultaneously, the optimal estimator gain matrix is formulated by minimizing the resulting state estimation error covariance. Additionally, sufficient conditions are introduced to guarantee the boundedness of the time estimation error covariance matrix. Then an optimal power allocation scheme under power limited conditions is obtained using the above results. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed SF state estimation strategy is demonstrated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Standardized Design Method of Main Circulation Frame for Offshore Platform Cooling Systems*
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a standardized design procedure of main circulation frame for offshore platform cooling systems. Offshore platform converter valve cooling system uses seawater circulation cooling cycle of the two-cycle cooling mode. The cooling of the seawater circulation cooling system uses the seawater plate heat exchanger to take away the cooling device cycle heat. Due to the offshore construction projects on the cooling amount of demand becomes larger, and gradually used seawater cycle fresh water cycle cooling cycle is a three-cycle cooling mode, the three cycles are internal circulation cooling system, fresh water cycle and seawater cycle. Internal circulation cooling system cooling medium for deionized water. Then, the system is directly strung into the converter valve, transformer heat exchanger to absorb its heat dissipation. Fresh water circulation cooling system cooling medium uses the fresh water plate heat exchanger to take away the internal circulation cooling system heat. Seawater circulation cooling system cooling medium for seawater uses the seawater plate heat exchanger to take away the freshwater cycle heat. With the change of cooling method, the structure configuration and control system of the whole cooling system are also optimized to provide a safe and stable cooling environment for the normal operation of the offshore HVDC platform.

articleTitle: Adaptive-triggered optimal sliding-mode control for nonlinear systems via disturbances observer
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This article focuses on a novel event-triggered sliding-mode control (SMC) problem for nonlinear system with interference through robust adaptive dynamic programming (ADP). The controller proposed in this paper is composed of discontinuous and continuous parts. For the discontinuous part of the controller, the disturbance is estimated according to the approximate structure of neural network (NN), and then the SMC is designed according to the adaptive dynamic triggering strategy (ADTS). What's more, the ADTS is optimized to self-triggering strategy with the aim to avoid the real-time measurement of the triggering conditions. For the continuous part of the controller, the optimal controller is designed according to the performance index function. At the same time, based on the ADP algorithm, the single critic NN is used to approximate the cost function, and the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation is solved to obtain the optimal controller. Moreover, via the Lyapunov technique, the uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB) stability conditions of the NN weight estimation error and sliding-mode dynamics are presented. In the end, simulation results verify the validity of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Visual-LIDAR SLAM Based on Supervised Hierarchical Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Deep learning has become increasingly crucial in simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Supervised deep learning SLAM methods need ground truth data for training but achieve highly accurate predictions. Such training techniques are used by some visual or LiDAR SLAM methods. However, these methods mostly rely on single-sensor data, missing the combined advantages of LiDAR and visual information. Multisensor fusion SLAM merges diverse data types, enriching features and boosting performance. This paper presents a new deep visual-LiDAR SLAM method that integrates both visual and LiDAR data. The SLAM system includes a deep visual-LiDAR odometry module, a deep learning-based loop closure detection module, and a 3D mapping module. The deep visual-LiDAR odometry module uses a hierarchical feature encoding module to capture features from two frames of color point clouds at various levels. An attention feature decoding module employs an attention mechanism to merge these features, determining their relative pose. The iterative pose optimization module continuously refines the pose accuracy, improving robustness to outliers. The loop closure detection module uses a deep learning-based global descriptor for precise positional matching. The 3D mapping module constructs the environmental map. Experimental results on the KITTI odometry dataset show that our method outperforms other supervised and traditional geometric methods, with lower rotation and translation errors. By integrating visual and LiDAR data, our SLAM system achieves higher accuracy and robustness in pose estimation compared to single-modal SLAM systems.

articleTitle: LQR control design for virtual inertia of new energy: A GA-assisted design method
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of new energy generation in the power grid, the inertia level and anti-interference ability of the power grid have been affected to a certain extent. New energy generation (wind power, solar power, energy storage) does not have inertia like traditional synchronous machine generation. Essentially, these new energy generation methods do not have inertia, which can lead to a decrease in the inertia level of the power grid system, thereby affecting the stability of the system. However, if a certain virtual inertia control strategy is added to new energy generation, they will also provide a certain amount of inertia for the system, just like traditional synchronous machines. This article mainly studies the new energy virtual inertia control strategy based on the LQR algorithm. By studying the dynamic characteristics of virtual synchronous machines, quantitative expressions for inertia parameters and system frequency response characteristics are obtained. On the other hand, genetic algorithm is introduced to optimize the parameters of LQR control algorithm, hoping to achieve better control effect. Finally, at the end of this article, the benefits and practicality of the proposed control method were verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: TAST-GCN: Topology Adaptive Spatial-Temporal GCN for traffic accidents prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Traffic accidents usually lead to bodily injury and economic loss. Accurate prediction help to prevent accidents happening and lower possible loss. However, urban traffic condition is effected by complex factors such as road infrastructure, traffic flow speed and adverse weather conditions. Thus, accidents prediction is a challenging task. To solve above problems, we proposed TAST-GCN. TAST-GCN contains three module: spatial module, spatial-temporal module, natural FC module. Spatial module performs graph convolution operations to learn spatial correlations. Spatial-temporal module utilizes graph convolution and temporal pooling to learn spatial-temporal correlations. Natural FC module aims to obtain meaningful representations of natural weather data. To evaluate the proposed model, wide range of real-world data, including weather, traffic flow, POI, road networks and accidents historical records are collected. Experiments on real-world dataset prove that TAST-GCN outperforms traditional and state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: An optimized fuzzy PI control method utilizing the IGWO algorithm for the ejector-based hydrogen recirculation PEMFC system
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Research on modeling and control strategies of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) system is pivotal for enhancing their performance and operational lifespan. In this study, the anode pressure control challenge within the hydrogen recirculation system of fuel cells is tackled by proposing a fuzzy PI control method optimized with an improved grey wolf optimization (IGWO) algorithm. Initially, a dynamic model of the ejector-based hydrogen recirculation PEMFC system is developed. To address the tendency that the traditional GWO algorithm falls into local optima, enhancements including an adjusted convergence factor and the integration of Gaussian mutation and a greedy algorithm are introduced, which are then applied to optimize the parameters of the fuzzy PI controller. By utilizing MATLAB/Simulink platform, a model for the PEMFC hydrogen recirculation system is developed and subjected to simulation studies. The results of the simulation suggest that, compared to traditional PID and fuzzy PI controllers, the proposed method shows improvements in terms of settling time (less than 1 s) and overshoot (less than 1%), along with enhanced robustness, Ensuring the sustained and dependable operation of the PEMFC over the long term.

articleTitle: Single-Class Detection Method for Bar Material Surface Defects Based on Self-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of surface defect detection in steel bars, proposing a one-class method based on self-supervised learning and thoroughly explores its effectiveness in online detection scenarios. Due to the limited number and incomplete variety of defect samples in the actual production environment, the traditional deep learning algorithms that rely on supervised learning face great challenges. On the contrary, defect-free samples are abundant and easy to obtain, so the single-classification task trained with single-class samples is more suitable for this scenario. In this study, normal samples were enhanced by DotPaste, PatchPaste and LinePaste to generate pseudo-samples with similar defect samples, which supports the self-supervised learning framework to train the model without real defect samples. At the same time, the class activation mapping (CAM) technology is introduced to realize the accurate positioning of defect positions. After experimental verification, the method proposed in this paper performs excellent in the surface defect detection of steel bars. The AUC value reaches 0.9934, which is significantly better than the traditional method, effectively solving the problem of scarce defect samples, and providing an efficient and reliable solution for the online detection of the surface defects of steel bars.

articleTitle: Dynamic-Encoding-Based Sliding Mode Control Under Round-Robin Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This article investigates the sliding mode control problem based on dynamic encoding-decoding over lossy networks with Round-Robin (RR) protocol. Firstly, considering non-encoded transmission, the sliding mode controller gain and the sliding mode region are acquired over in case of lossy networks under RR protocol. Then, considering encoded transmission, state-dependent online adjustment rules are introduced, and a dynamic-quantization-based encoding-decoding scheme is designed. Pre-designed sliding mode controller is proven to be feasible even with limited encoding length. However, due to inevitable encoding errors, the convergence domain and sliding mode region of the closed-loop system both increase. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is verified by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Registration Network Based on Daul-Attention Mechanism For Truck Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Truck pose estimation is a pivotal technology for automating excavation and loading processes in intelligent mining excavators. The existing methods for pose estimation are mainly based on sensor measurements and traditional registration techniques. While these sensor-based methods can identify truck poses, they are prone to significant cumulative errors due to factors like vibrations and also suffer from short sensor lifespans. Traditional registration methods use iterative closest point algorithms to estimate the bucket’s pose by aligning its point clouds, but these methods are prone to getting stuck in local optima. Recently, deep learning-based networks for object pose estimation have been introduced. However, in the mining operation environment, the truck’s position changes significantly during the loading process, leading to distinct truck features at different poses. Traditional point cloud registration networks often just concatenate the features of template and target point clouds, which inadequately exploits both global and local features. This limitation decreases the accuracy of truck pose estimation. To tackle the feature fusion challenge, we introduce a novel feature fusion registration network named CASNet. CASNet consists of a feature extraction module, a feature fusion module, and a pose computation module. The feature fusion module employs spatial and channel attention mechanisms to effectively learn different hierarchical features during feature fusion. By integrating both local and global features, CASNet addresses feature fusion issues and enhances generalization capabilities. Experimental results show that our method significantly reduces both rotational and translational errors in truck pose estimation by 1.26° and 2.74 cm, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel LiDAR-Inertial SLAM with Low Accumulation Error
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Existing LiDAR-based SLAM frameworks typically consist of a frontend odometry and a backend global optimization. The frontend performs real-time ego-motion estimation through point cloud registration, while the backend involves graph optimization and pose smoothing at a lower frequency. To further minimize cumulative error, we enhance the LiDAR-IMU SLAM algorithm. The frontend focuses on estimating relative poses within a local map centered on keyframes by a step-by-step optimization approach, while the backend corrects keyframe poses based on global optimality criteria by integrating ground feature information, loop closure, and a priori maps into the factor graph. The real-time pose output is achieved by merging the optimization results from both modules. Experimental validation is conducted using both public and self-collected datasets. Qualitative and quantitative trajectory analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of our method in reducing cumulative error and ensuring robustness. Furthermore, our algorithm facilitates the expansion of point cloud maps. By partitioning the scene into partially overlapping sub-regions, we can gradually construct large-scale point cloud maps.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Two-wheeled Self-Balancing Robot based on LQR
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The two-wheeled self-balancing robot is a typical under-actuated system, which has the characteristics of nonlinearity, multivariable, strong coupling and high instability. This paper constructs a relatively precise mathematical model for the two-wheeled self-balancing robot system by applying the Newton-Euler method, specifically tailored to its unique characteristics. Then, based on this model, a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controller is designed, and the theoretical effectiveness of the LQR controller is verified through simulation experiments. On this basis, this paper further proposes a practical control scheme for practical applications, and elaborates on the implementation details based on the LQR controller. The experimental results show that this control scheme exhibits excellent control performance, providing a computationally efficient, low-cost, and effective solution for others to implement two-wheeled self-balancing robot.

articleTitle: A comprehensive PEMFC system model integrating metal hydride hydrogen storage tank
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: A novel approach to constructing an integrated thermal management system (ITMS) for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) and metal hydride (MH) tanks was proposed. The MH will release hydrogen when absorbing heat. Fuel cell waste heat could be used to heat the MH tank, reducing the load on the radiator and making the system more efficient. Based on the fuel cell system’s vital reaction process and core components, a comprehensive system simulation model with gas-heat-electricity coupling was built. The PEMFC stack, MH hydrogen supply, air supply, stack temperature management, MH tank temperature management, and charge air temperature management are all represented in this model. With the system integrated, different thermal processes were coordinated through rational and effective control of the power unit and thermal components. Finally, the dynamic response analysis of the system showed that the model could effectively simulate the thermal and hydraulic behaviour of the fuel cell system, including how critical parameters like mass flow, pressure, and temperature spread out. The constructed model laid the foundation for developing efficiency-optimized thermoelectric control strategies and fault detection. Also, the performance parameters of the stack and thermal components can be changed to create a system model with higher power output.

articleTitle: Design of Virtual Simulation Experiment for Semiconductor Oxidation Process Based on Unity3D
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In response to the challenges of complex teaching content, high safety risks, high economic costs, and low student interest in semiconductor process experiments, a virtual simulation experiment project for the semiconductor oxidation process was developed. This project, which is based on the Unity3D engine and virtual reality technology, uses key equipment and process flows as simulation objects. The technology has been used to design twin three-dimensional equipment models, simulation interactive components, and process mechanism algorithms. This has led to the development of a semiconductor oxidation process virtual simulation experiment system. The system offers virtual reality interactive operations, process parameter settings, experimental data access, and other functions, thereby providing a highly immersive and safe interaction environment for experimental teaching in professional courses. This effectively enhances the quality and impact of experimental teaching in these courses.

articleTitle: A soft actor-critic based method for two manipulators coordinated lifting and balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Robotic arms are widely used in industrial fields because of their flexibility and satisfactory scalability. With the development of robotics, the demand for multi-robotic arm collaborative control tasks in the industry is also increasing. Maintaining balance during the coordinated lifting of objects by two robotic arms is not only beneficial to the protection of objects but also reduces the load of each robotic arm to achieve safe and effective results. The task described in this article requires two robotic arms to coordinatedly lift a pot and maintain the ball in the center of the pot. For this multi-objective task, problem difficulty and solution time increase, and the design of the strategy becomes complex. Reinforcement learning has the advantage of learning trajectory planning strategies on its own. In this article, an offline control strategy based on soft actor-critic (SAC) is introduced. This strategy can successfully solve the coordinated balanced lifting problem of two manipulators in a simulation environment. The strategy achieves a high success rate.

articleTitle: Vehicular Platoon Control Using Traffic Flow Information from Road Network
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, the control problem of connection vehicles in the city is investigated. The network traffic flow is managed using an Autonomous Intersection Management (AIM) platform, and a hierarchical control framework is also proposed to model the network topology on a non-directed graph, in which traffic information can be exchanged through the Infrastructure-to-Infrastructure(I2I) communication. This consistency algorithm is used to coordinate the traffic information of adjacent intersections. The relationship between traffic flow and traffic density is considered. Based on the traffic flow model, the desired velocity and spacing are obtained. The PID controller shall be constructed such that the required distance between the vehicles is kept at the same speed as the leader. The simulation results show that the designed controller keeps the following car on track with the leader under time delay.

articleTitle: Hardware-Accelerated Real-Time Detection of Catenary Geometry Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Dynamic detection of catenary geometry parameters (CGP) has a significant impact on the stability of the train power supply. Aiming at the problem that the detection speed of traditional detection methods can not meet the high frequency, high speed, and low fitness, this paper presents a non-contact, high-precision, real-time detection system for the CGP based on FPGA hardware acceleration. Dynamic measurement techniques based on monocular cameras and line-structured light. Firstly, the FPGA controls the camera to acquire images in real-time, and a parallel three-step median filtering algorithm is developed to reduce image noise, ten times more efficiently than the traditional median filter. Secondly, in order to solve the catenary localization problem in complex scenes, Hough transform is utilized to detect catenary, and the mean-shift algorithm is improved according to the hardware structure to realize catenary localization and tracking in complex scenes. Additionally, the weighted centroid extraction algorithm combined with hardware acceleration is optimized to achieve the stable extraction of pixel coordinates. Finally, the FPGA migration of the algorithms is completed. The coordinates of the spot center are transmitted to the host via Ethernet, and CGP is calculated by reconstructing the line structured light in 3D. After testing an image with a resolution of 800*480, Modelsim simulation takes 0.02 ms to process one image frame. When the algorithm is transplanted to the FPGA platform, the process from sending the control word to receiving the center of mass coordinates takes only 25 ms. The experiments demonstrate that the detection system outlined in this paper exhibits high accuracy and speed, adaptability, portability, and ease of installation, making it highly valuable for practical applications.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Control of Networked Systems with Quantized Measurements Under Try-Once-Discard Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the data-driven control problem for a networked systems with try-once-discard (TOD) protocol and quantization effect. To begin with, we establish a data-based input-output model based on the data collected in a prior experiment. A so-called TOD protocol is adopted to schedule the measurement data of sensors for the purpose of avoiding data collisions, under which only one sensor is permitted to access to the network at each transmission instant. In addition, the measurement data would be quantized before transimission. The objective of this paper is to present a design for an output-feedback controller such that the system output is exponentially ultimately bounded. By utilizing linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), a sufficient condition is guaranteed for the design of the controller. Finally, a numerical simulation is provided to illustrate the effectiveness and validity of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Finite Horizon ℋ∞ State Estimation with Packet Losses over Half-Duplex Relay Networks : Handling Amplify-and-Forward Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, the finite horizon ℋ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> state estimation problem is addressed for a class of time-varying nonlinear systems with packet losses over half-duplex (HD) relay communication network. To enhance the quality of long-distance signal transmission, an HD relay-aided strategy is adopted to forward the transmitted signals between sensors and remote state estimators, in which the forwarding protocol is amplify-and-forward (AaF) protocol. Three Bernoulli random variables are utilized to characterize the packet losses phenomenon in the communication process between sensors and remote estimators. A sufficient condition is firstly derived to ensure the existence of finite horizon state estimator meeting ℋ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance constraint. Then the desired gain parameters are calculated in terms of resolving a set of recursive linear matrix inequalities (RLMIs). Finally, a simulation example is given to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed state estimation scheme.

articleTitle: Road Disease Damage Detection Based on Improved CenterNet
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Road damage detection is an important step in ensuring road safety and achieving timely repair of road damage, which is of great significance in reducing road maintenance costs. Deep learning technology has developed rapidly this year, and using computer vision technology instead of manual detection can achieve automated detection of road losses. However, there are still a series of problems such as low detection efficiency and poor image quality. In response to the above issues, in this article, we first established a road dataset, including 2575 Chinese road images and 3589 road damage annotations. Then, we proposed an improved model based on CenterNet, using the Asymptotic Feature Pyramid structure. Using this method, we fused two adjacent low-level features, and gradually fused the high-level features. In the feature fusion process, adaptive spatial fusion is utilized to avoid multi-target information conflict, and then the CLA cross-layer attention mechanism is utilized to improve the performance of small-target detection in the model and reduce the computational amount of the model. Finally, it is experimentally demonstrated that our improvement improves the detection accuracy and the computational cost is within a manageable range.

articleTitle: Research on 6DOF Pose Measurement Algorithm of Industrial Metal Workpiece Based on Binocular Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In the face of the promotion of robot positioning and grasping applications in the industrial field, accurate identification and positioning of target objects in complex industrial environments have become a research highlights. To solve the problem of visual positioning interference caused by local reflections on industrial metal workpieces and obtain high-precision pose measurement results, this paper proposes a binocular vision 6DOF pose measurement strategy. Firstly, in view of the difficulties in manually collecting images and the high cost of collection, a data augmentation method based on generative adversarial networks is applied to achieve data augmentation and expand the the metal object image datasets. Then, in response to the problem of deformation and missing target objects in the images generated by the image data augmentation model, this paper proposes a method of changing the model architecture to improve the model's feature extraction ability for target objects and enrich the detailed features of the output images. Finally, aiming at the problem that the reflection of metal workpieces leads to incomplete information collection of the target object by the visual system and affects the pose measurement, this paper proposes a deep learning-based multi-keypoint detection method to provide effective data input for binocular vision 6DOF pose measurement. Combined with the binocular vision triangulation method to obtain the three-dimensional information of the target object, the pose measurement accuracy of the target object's 6DOF is improved. Experimental results show that this strategy outputs pose measurement data with high accuracy, providing data support for binocular vision-guided robot positioning and grasping.

articleTitle: l1 Filtering for Multirate Positive Systems With Weighted Try-Once-Discard Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In this paper, the (partial) l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> filtering problem of a class of positive multirate systems is studied under the scheduling of the weighted try-once-discard (WTOD) communication protocol. Firstly, the multirate system is transformed into a single-rate model by utilizing the iterative state equation method. The signal transmission between the sensor nodes and the filter is carried out in wireless communication networks. In order to reduce the communication burden and avoid the possible network congestion, the WTOD protocol is used to schedule the transmission sequence of the sensor nodes. Secondly, filters are designed in both the general form and the observer-based form. In addition, sufficient criteria are provided by the co-positive Lyapunov function method, which ensures the existence of the filters as well as the exponential stability and specified l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-gain performance index of the filtering error systems. Additionally included are the explicit design approaches for the filter gain matrices. Lastly, a numerical example is provided to confirm the usefulness of the suggested outcomes.

articleTitle: Multi-objective capacity configuration optimization of a grid-connected SOFC/LB microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: The solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) technique with electric to gas technique is an investment-worthy way to enhance the consumption of renewable energy in microgrids. Moreover, SOFC’s high fuel adaptability and efficient cogeneration are ideal for stationary power generation. However, due to SOFC’s slow load response and high cost, the capacity configuration designation of microgrid with SOFC system is significant. To enhance energy utilization and reduce cost, in this paper, a microgrid connected with an upper grid, containing SOFC, wind turbine (WT), photovoltaics (PV), electrolyzer, a hydrogen storage system (HSS), and lithium battery (LB), is built. Considering the dynamic characteristics of SOFC’s load response, transient and steady-stage’s energy management strategies assisted by LB are proposed. Capacity configuration parameters of microgrid’s components are selected as decision variables and minimal life cycle cost (LCC) and minimal curtailment rate of wind and PV are selected as objective functions. Using proposed strategies to process microgrids, the NSGA-II algorithm is used to optimize. An actual case is studied and appropriate capacity configuration is solved, with 2112 120W PVs,315 500W WTs, 5 10kW • h LBs,5 SOFCs,98.73kW electrolyzer and 38.94kg HSS.LCC reaches $4.268 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and wind &PV’s curtailment rate reaches 5.71%. The result’s rationality is proved by analyzing the detailed cost and operation.

articleTitle: Computation Offloading Based on Unscented Transform Biogeography-based Optimization in Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Computation offloading, as one of the means to reduce latency and energy consumption in mobile edge computing (MEC), can significantly reduce communication costs and enhance resource utilization. In response to compute-intensive and latency-sensitive application scenarios, an unscented transform biogeography-based optimization (UTBBO) algorithm is proposed to the facilitate computation offloading of MEC. Building upon classical migration and mutation strategies, UTBBO utilizes a guiding strategy with unscented transform to finely develop elite individuals within the visible range of the search domain, thereby avoiding the algorithm from falling into local optima. Furthermore, a computation offloading system encompassing cloud, edge, and terminal devices is established, and the offloading tasks are transformed into the optimization process of the cost function using UTBBO, where the cost function is a weighted sum of latency and energy consumption. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed UTBBO algorithm can effectively reduce latency and energy consumption in computation offloading tasks across multiple scenarios in edge computing, providing more rational offloading decisions.

articleTitle: Integrated energy system scheduling considering carbon trading price demand response
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: In a dual-carbon context, multi-energy coupling technology can absorb wind and solar energy, and carbon trading can control carbon emissions, thus accelerating the process of achieving 'carbon neutrality'. This paper proposes an integrated energy system scheduling model to address the impacts of carbon trading prices, wind power, solar power, load, and other uncertainties on energy scheduling. A technique for demand response based on carbon trading price is proposed to minimize the impact of price fluctuations caused by carbon trading. The model considers factors such as equipment operating costs, carbon trading costs, demand response costs, and wind and solar abandonment costs. Multiple energy storage technologies are utilized to enhance the flexibility of the dispatch strategy. The article introduces information gap decision theory to solve the model for multi-energy scheduling, considering its economy and robustness. The scheduling scenarios for a typical day are analyzed under risk-averse and risk-seeking strategies. The results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the total cost by 26.3% compared to the baseline scenario, validating the effectiveness of the proposed scheduling strategy.

articleTitle: The Necessary and Sufficient Condition for SDP Relaxation to be Tight in MVDR Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of solving the minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) robust adaptive beamforming (RAB) by estimating the steering vector of the signal-of-interest (SOI). And this issue can be reformulated as a homogeneous quadratic constrained quadratic programming (HQCQP). We derive the optimal solution of its relaxation by SDP, and subsequently propose methods to figure out its tightness and then achieve a globally optimal solution for HQCQP. It should be noted that a solution with rank one is not guaranteed in existing literatures. Leveraging the recent advancements in SDP, namely, a condition that serves as both a sufficient and necessary test, we verify if the SDP relaxation is tight and then propose effective algorithms to address the problem. Two specific instances of the MVDR have been modeled. Numerical experiments are presented, illustrating the high ratioof the presence of a solution with rank one in the MVDR scenario, and the robust adaptive beamformer with respect to output SINR performs well.

articleTitle: An Active Contour Model Based on Local Entropy for Image Segmentation with High Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Active contour models (ACMs) have been employed extensively in the area of image segmentation. Howbeit, ACMs exist some disadvantages including slow evolution, sensitivity to intensity inhomogeneity and noise. Therefore, an ACM based on local entropy is put forward to segment images with high noise and inhomogeneous intensity. Specifically, the local entropy fitting image is firstly introduced to constrict different noise kinds and levels when preserving image detail information. The bias correction energy formulation is constructed through employing the local entropy fitting image to estimate bias field for better correcting the massive inhomogeneous intensity distribution. Finally, an enhanced regularization term and the average filtering are applied to eliminate instability in numerical calculations during the evolution of level set function. The comparative experiments conducted on synthetic and real images with high noise and intensity heterogeneity indicate the better accuracy and robustness of the introduced model.

articleTitle: Optimization algorithm and application of sand cat swarm based on sparrow warning mechanism and spiral search strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 39th Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
